title: Developer Platform Consoles Should Be Dumb
abstract: Most of the developer platform consoles I saw are getting it completely wrong, and I honestly cannot understand why. For decades now we know that a good UI is a dumb UI. A good UI does not contain much logic. UIs rely on APIs to discover what can be done and what information is needed to do whatever should be done. Yet, when I see developer portal UIs, more often than not, they do not try to rely on APIs. Instead, they are doing their best to ignore them, to bypass them, to use their internal APIs, and to do too much for no good reason.

abstract: In the course of several SaaS migrations to Otel and Prom-based exporters, the search for the perfect PromQL CPU Usage (and Mem Usage) query ended up with several candidates. This quick talk will walk through these queries, explain their differences, and offer the crowd a way to rate the queries and vote on which ones they think should be used. A quick search on Stack Overflow will also produce quite a few queries to use and prove the need for some crowdsourcing on what queries should be the standard. Let's let the people decide! Or at least let's understand the appropriateness of various queries versus other options; how container and various prometheus exporter metrics work; and talk about the challenges of observability migrations with regards to translating queries from difference vendors to Open Source telemetry. Queries include cadvisor metrics, kubestate metrics, and node exporter metrics -- which also probably adds to the chaos of why there are so many cpu/mem queries.

abstract:

We'll explore the exciting ChatGPT world, building an efficient data pipeline that's enriched with vector embeddings as stored in a vector DB (PgVector) , and how it can pair with the performant RisingWave cloud-based stream processor for its write job. We will illustrate a sample use case with live coding, as follows:

* Simulate a streaming data feed from X (or Twitter), we'll be using Kafka as the message broker for data ingestion
* RisingWave will consume the data stream, and perform data analysis
* Construct prompts based on the top 3 hashtags identified by RisingWave
* Prompts will be used for inferencing against a RAG-based BOT built with PgVector

title: Stop Deploying Blind! Using Observability and Argo Rollouts to Light the Way
abstract:

Did you always want to deploy on Friday afternoon and go straight to the pub? Many teams perform “blind” deployments without any real insight into what will be affected by the new application version. Consequently, they don’t have enough data to understand the blast radius of a release and whether to decide if it was successful or not. Even companies that have several metrics in place, don’t always use them in an automated manner. Wouldn’t it be great if you could see user behavior with new features in real time and identify performance bottlenecks before a full release?

title: So You Want to Write Memory with eBPF?
abstract: A lot of eBPF programs fall into the category of observing the Linux system, i.e the kernel, system libraries or user-space programs. For the purpose of observing the system, we mostly rely on reading memory with eBPF, either kernel or user-space memory. However, sometimes various eBPF use cases require writing memory, for example propagating W3C context for various application protocols. This talk focuses on our journey to implement W3C trace context propagation with eBPF at various levels of the protocol stack. We explore what memory write eBPF APIs are available to us today, along with their implications to system security, stability, required permissions and implementation difficulty. We’ll present two working solutions with their pros and cons, a lot of dead ends, as well as explore what a new approach might look like by leveraging the “BPF arena” feature in kernel 6.9.

title: Incremental GPU Slicing in Action
abstract: Large language models are often released as families of models with varying parameter counts and quantization. To reduce cost, inference services increasingly rely on dynamic model selection, preferring smaller models when possible. GPU vendors are on a journey to enable dynamic GPU slicing, making it possible for a workload to request a fraction of the compute and memory units in a GPU, and for the slices to be created and destroyed on demand without disrupting existing workloads. The onus is now on Kubernetes. The Device Management Working Group is hard at work to expose these capabilities. While vendor-agnostic slicing APIs do not exist yet, this talk demonstrates that incremental GPU slicing is possible today. We replace the Multi-Instance GPU manager, which only permits partitioning GPUs in bulk, with an open-source incremental-slicing controller without needing new APIs or changes to the device plugin. Come learn how to achieve incremental slicing in your GPU clusters.

title: From Sensors to Servers: Efficient Edge Computing with Akri and WebAssembly
abstract: At the edge, thousands of sensors publish data. Servers on the edge must discover these devices and then continually process new data from them. Akri and SpinKube are open source projects that address these challenges, providing a seamless experience for connecting IoT devices to Kubernetes clusters at the edge. Akri discovers these devices and automatically deploys Pods to consume their data. SpinKube runs serverless WebAssembly (Wasm) applications as Pods on Kubernetes. Since Wasm has small binary sizes and sub-millisecond start up times, it's the ideal application type for resource constrained servers at the edge. This presentation will conclude with a demo of using Akri to discover MQTT-based devices and automatically deploy Wasm applications to the cluster. The deployed applications will be event-driven and triggered by new MQTT messages, ensuring precise resource usage. By the end of the talk, you'll have the tools to run efficient data processing applications at the edge.
session_types: Kubernetes on Edge Day/Event + Data Collection

title: Enabling Intelligent Observability Volume Management
abstract: Ensuring observability is critical, especially as operations expand into edge cloud environments. Effective observability data volume management is crucial to benefit from observability while controlling costs (storage, network, processing). Naive data reduction (e.g.,changing all metrics freq from 30s to 5min, sampling traces) can harm SLAs. With Observability Volume Manager(OVM), IBM and RedHat have co-developed an open-source intelligent framework with dynamic, fine-grained control of observability data volume. It works across modalities and integrates with open-source tools like Prometheus and OTel. OVM performs dynamic transformations at edge like filtering/aggregating data to reduce volume as well as adjust metric frequency/log levels for risk based zoom in/out and issue triaging. OVM identifies highly correlated/computed metrics and performs intelligent pruning and given an observability budget, identifies the subset of metrics and frequencies to minimize downstream task impact.
session_types: Observability Day/Managing the Ever-increasing Volume of Observability Data

title: Panel: Startups With Open Source Projects: Can They Be Successful in the CNCF? And Should They Be?
abstract:
The CNCF hosts a wide variety of open source projects, not just in functionality but in the nature of the maintainers and funders behind the project. Some projects are backed by multiple large companies, including public companies with trillion-dollar market caps. Some are backed by single small startups with a small fraction of the resources. And some projects fall somewhere in between. But all share one fact: the vast majority of contributions are done by paid maintainers.
For startups in the CNCF ecosystem, is it possible to be successful delivering a CNCF open source project? Or is this strategy a fundamentally un-monetizable one? And from the perspective of the cloud native community, is it actually important for startups to be successful in this community? Or should the CNCF primarily focus on projects that are more like Kubernetes itself—backed by well-established companies with the resources and longevity to keep their projects afloat indefinitely?
Join this panel to hear from startup founders, project maintainers, and others in the thick of the struggle between commercialization and open source, between paying maintainers and appealing to the open source.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: LLM-Driven Applications: Intro to LLM Agents in Kubernetes
abstract: Over the past year, there has been a lot of important work and discussions around how to run Large Language Models (LLMs) on top of Kubernetes. But what happens once you have your LLM running in your cluster? How can you build an application around your LLM, where the LLM can act as an agent and call out to various services you have deployed in your cluster to solve complex tasks that would otherwise cause the LLM to hallucinate? Is there a way to do this without making changes to the services and deployments already in your cluster? In this talk I will be exploring what an LLM agent is and how you build an agent that will call out to your services. I will show this with a demo of an LLM agent running in a kubernetes cluster that is able to automatically detect new tools and agents deployed to the cluster and coordinate them to complete complex tasks in a conversation with the user.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: Global Tenant Management Using Argo
abstract: For the Collibra data intelligence platform, a tenant is a combination of applications provisioned on a mixture of virtual machines and single—and multi-tenant Kubernetes services. This combination makes tenant lifecycle management non-trivial. In this session, we’ll explore using Argo Events, Workflows, and CD to build a global tenant management system. The system supports tenant lifecycle events like create, update, suspend, backup, and restore across various application types and infrastructure without exposing Argo-specific constructs to the application teams. This abstraction, called bridged workflows, allows teams to hook into the lifecycles in a simple Kubernetes native way, providing operations and developers the same simple participation in the global tenant management lifecycle. The case study will give you ideas for building a global tenant management system using the Argo suite.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: Ranking Argo CD Settings in a Tier List
abstract: Argo CD has a lot of settings and this has only proliferated in each new release of Argo CD. In this talk we will review many of these settings and values using the always fun and informative concept of the Tier List. Tiers for the settings/values include “Make this the default”, “Almost always useful”, “Good in places”, “Meh?” and finally “Nobody needs this”. Audience participation will be encouraged in this session with audience members helping to rank settings and values by show of hands.

Since we're not frontend experts, we needed a framework that allows us to build a dashboard with minimal effort, is customizable, and offers an ecosystem of extensibility--all of which Backstage provides. Moreover, the Software Catalog and Software Templates core plugins in Backstage align well with the application-centric development model that Radius aims to provide, making it a natural choice for building the Radius Dashboard. This talk will explore how the team leveraged the Backstage platform to accelerate development of the Radius Dashboard, and how the plugin implementations of the Radius application graph visualizations paves the way for deeper integrations within the Backstage ecosystem.

Imagine an automated approach that seamlessly deploys and configures these devices in real-time. GitOps has emerged as a leading trend to facilitate collaboration, configuration, and deployment of intricate and dynamic applications. Join us for this session where we present our solution for deploying dynamic IoT applications over a Private 5G network in a hybrid cloud environment. This session will give details on how the integration of CNCF projects such as Nephio, and Akri can transform your IoT management through the adoption of GitOps principles.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: Searching for Serverless Candidates in the Jungle of Microservices
abstract: Everyone wants a judicial use of resources - and serverless computing makes it happen by limiting the idle resources. While services with clear functional use cases are developed as one, more often than not such benefits are not clear - such as unclear or changing application usage patterns. Similarly several historical services could now be suited for serverless functions based on they way they are actually used. However they are rarely investigated because their impact remains opaque - a lack of cost/performance benefits and whether re-architecture effort is justified. In this talk, the Yash will showcase a case study about how they went researching for serverless candidates in their real world systems and how surprising the results were. He will also showcase the impact and key learnings - how turning even lightweight microservices into serverless functions helped saved significantly on infra costs AND, also improving the peak load performance of several unrelated services!

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: How GitOps Changes Identity and RBAC Management
abstract: ArgoCD pulls and applies resources from Git repositories, CI/CD pipelines act based on events emitted by repositories, and developers interact with and debug the resources managed by both. Unfortunately, GitOps controllers, CI/CD pipelines, and developers all have different identities and different RBAC models. How can we find harmony in these approaches and effectively manage permissions across them? We’ll show how we’re using OAuth2-Token Exchange (RFC 8693) with Dex and GitHub Teams with ArgoCD AppProjects to provide consistent permissions to repositories, people, and CI pipelines with just OIDC. We also show how we designed a just-in-time RBAC approach by programmatically managing the ArgoCD AppProjects based on the repository manifests.

This session aims to provide a comprehensive, step-by-step guide on interacting with Argo Workflows using Fabric8’s Custom Resource Definitions (CRD) in Java. Argo Workflows are implemented as 'Custom Resources' in Kubernetes. By leveraging the Fabric8 library’s Custom Resource Definitions, developers can seamlessly interact with Argo Workflows through the Kubernetes API. Join us to learn how to harness the power of Argo Workflows in Java, simplifying your workflow management on Kubernetes.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: Countercultural: Backstage for Consultants
abstract: In 1914, Booz Allen Hamilton pioneered the field of management consulting. Today, we are trusted as the largest provider of AI to the federal government. Our goal is to provide technically differentiated solutions that solve complex client problems at scale, and to do that, we are championing a culture of internal reuse. This includes applying InnerSource principles, through a Backstage developer portal, to improve velocity, quality, and DevEx for a technical workforce of 14,000. InnerSource principles of transparency and self-service can be at odds with corporate hierarchy, program silos due to varied client contracts, and the “need to know” mindset required when handling classified information. To get the best of both worlds, our Backstage team has learned to lean into that tension and deploy change management techniques to build community and rally support for new ways of working. This session will explore corporate barriers to Backstage adoption and lessons learned along the way.

abstract: Applications at edge environment can be platform dependent, complicated and distributed in regions, and the number of devices significantly increases. Our final goal is to create the infrastructure that can be applied to the entire environment crossing over the cloud and edge in common. Working with KubeEdge and Cilium, we are now successfully able to use Cilium with KubeEdge hosted nodes at edge environment. This means, enabling wireguard VPN with Cilium can provide the transparent network connectivity with the nodes running in the cloud infrastructure, so that edge nodes running at edge environment just appear to be a member of cluster system but with edge autonomy feature provided by KubeEdge. We would like to share our technical insights and experience with using Cilium at edge with KubeEdge, and what are the future development and contribution with Cilium community.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: Cost Saving Strategies for Interactive AI Development
abstract: The interactive nature of Jupyter notebooks has made them indispensable tools for data scientists and AI researchers, facilitating exploratory data analysis, prototyping, and model development. However, managing the cost of resource-intensive computations at different stages of AI/ML lifecycle presents significant challenges. We leveraged Apache YuniKorn to design a resource management system tailored for notebook workloads, which incorporates fair sharing, user-specific policies and budget constraints to allocate computational resources efficiently while adapting for both data preparation and model training stages. And thanks to the extensibility of JupyterLab, we offer rich displays next to the Notebook enabling data scientists to introspect resource usage in real time. This session presents cost saving strategies for interactive development on Jupyter using Kubeflow for model training and Spark for data preparation with YuniKorn scheduler.

title: ⚡ Lightning Talk: The Merge Conflict - Conflict: Apply-Before-Merge vs. Traditional Continuous Deployment
abstract:
In modern infrastructure management, Terraform and now it's open source fork, OpenTofu, has emerged as a leading tool for Infrastructure as Code (IaC), enabling efficient and reproducible infrastructure deployments.

This talk explores two distinct approaches to integrating OpenTofu into your deployment pipeline: the approve-before-merge approach using Atlantis and the traditional continuous deployment (CD) strategy where changes are applied post-merge.

We’ll delve into the workflows, benefits, and challenges of each method, examining how they handle collaboration, ensure compliance, and manage deployment risks. Attendees will gain insights into choosing the right strategy for their teams, balancing speed and safety in their Terraform deployments.

title: Rewiring Cilium: Operator-Driven Scale and Security With CiliumEndpointSlice
abstract:
As clusters scale, the control plane often bears the brunt of the growing pains. But what if scale didn’t have to mean stress? In this session, we’ll explore the CiliumEndpointSlice feature that has enabled more scalable container networking and laid the foundation for future optimizations in the Cilium ecosystem.
We start by exploring the default Cilium configuration and the strain it places on the kube-apiserver at scale. Then, we explore how enabling CiliumEndpointSlice helped us unlock higher scale at AKS, with details on its design, how it works & the performance gains we observed. We also share our experiences with fine-tuning clusters at scale & the tradeoffs involved. Finally, we take a glimpse at what’s next in the quest to centralize the Operator and make policy enforcement in Cilium more scalable.
Whether you're running Cilium at scale or just getting started, this talk will equip you with practical insights and architectural strategies to run high-scale Cilium clusters.

title: Beyond Chat: Bringing Agents To Kubernetes
abstract:

In this talk, we’ll introduce Kagent, a CNCF sandbox project offering a Kubernetes-native framework for building, deploying, and managing AI agents. Kagent makes it easy to define agents declaratively and manage them with familiar Kubernetes tools.

We’ll demo debugging agents built with Kagent that integrate with CNCF projects like Kubernetes, Argo, and Cilium. We’ll also show how Kagent supports flexible agent workflows across a variety of environments and use cases. Kagent provides a path to operationalize AI agents in cloud-native infrastructure, integrating with the CNCF ecosystem while supporting scalable, secure, and observable AI systems.

abstract:
This talk shows how to build an Envoy Gateway extension server, allowing you to define and implement custom GW-API extensions.

When talking about ingress, organizations often face a dilemma: build a bespoke control plane or adopt a CNCF project that may not fully meet their needs. Envoy Gateway offers a hybrid solution with a Kubernetes-native, standardized approach that covers most use cases but allows for customization via control plane extensibility.

Companies like SAP and Confluent, as well as OSS projects like Envoy AI Gateway, use this approach. They enhance Envoy Gateway with custom Gateway-API Policy Attachments and Filter Extensions, enabling custom behaviors in the proxy via xDS—from specific HTTP filters to tailored authorization logic. It’s powerful customization without starting from scratch.

We will explore the extension server's gRPC interface and its relation to Gateway API, and cover operational aspects such as deployment options, failure handling, and security.

We'll touch on actual PRs to chart our journey from simple documentation fixes to large-scale, high-impact feature deliveries.

We'll also explore how to advocate for and carve out time for open source contribution at your day job.

abstract:
Edge platforms are remote, resource-constrained, and mission-critical—making them ideal candidates for an immutable architecture. Edge environments demand resilience, security, and operational simplicity. This talk reimagines Kubernetes at the edge through a radical embrace of immutability, exploring how purpose-built, read-only operating systems, ephemeral workloads, and stateless infrastructure can transform the edge from a liability into a strength.
Inspired by Kundera’s existential lens, we’ll explore the philosophical and practical implications of immutability at the edge, using CNCF projects like k0s, Kairos, and Cluster API.we’ll architect a platform where every layer—from firmware to containers—is reproducible and replaceable, not mutable.
We'll see how Immutable builds can reduce attack surfaces, simplify updates, and achieve true zero-touch provisioning.
Join us to challenge the status quo—and embrace the lightness of being immutable.

title: Your AI Is a Toddler With Root Access: Why Kubernetes Policies Are Your Last Line of Defense
abstract:

As AI copilots and autonomous agents increasingly take the wheel in Kubernetes operations, we're witnessing a paradox: the very tools designed to eliminate human error are creating new categories of chaos at unprecedented scale. Your AI assistant doesn't get tired, doesn't need coffee breaks, and definitely doesn't read your runbooks. It can spawn a thousand misconfigured pods before you've finished reading this abstract.

This talk explores why Kubernetes admission policies (like Kyverno) must urgently evolve from "nice-to-have guardrails" to "absolutely critical blast doors" in the age of AI-driven operations.

title: Integrating Agentic AI Into Internal Developer Platforms To Minimize Errors and Downtime
abstract:

In this talk, we share how we enhanced our GitOps-based internal developer platform by integrating AI agents into the deployment workflow. Our platform uses the GitOps model to declaratively manage environments from Git, ensuring consistency and repeatability. However, the absence of semantic validation meant misconfigurations—such as resource requests exceeding quotas or Kyverno policy conflicts—would occasionally slip through. These issues led to failed scheduling, degraded availability, or blocked rollouts. Using kagent, our agents analyze the live cluster, Git state, and runtime config to detect semantic issues—like resource quota violations or Kyverno policy conflicts—and surface them in PRs with human-readable feedback.

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Mind the Topology: Smarter Scheduling for AI Workloads on Kubernetes
abstract:
AI workloads like distributed training, inference, and data preprocessing demand high bandwidth, low latency, and efficient access to accelerators – making topology-aware scheduling essential. This involves considering zones, racks, and device proximity when placing workloads. However, achieving this is complex due to the need to balance competing priorities like locality, fairness, and resource fragmentation across diverse workloads and dynamic cluster states. Kubernetes schedules pods independently and lacks a standard way to act on topological information, making it hard to balance locality, fairness, and resource use at scale.

This talk explores the challenges of topology-aware scheduling for AI on Kubernetes. We’ll review current solutions and their limitations, then show how the KAI Scheduler addresses these gaps with design choices that enable scalable, topology-aware workload placement.

title: Can We Really Parse DNS in eBPF? Improving Cilium ToFQDN With In-kernel Policy Updates
abstract:
Parsing DNS in eBPF has been “tricky” for a long time. One needs to handle DNS compression, follow an unknown number of pointers and parse an unknown number of answers. Things get complicated with DNS over TCP. What if the DNS response is split across multiple packets requiring us to parse TCP streams in eBPF ? Luckily eBPF is now sufficiently advanced to handle such complex logic.

So, what does this mean for toFQDN policies in CIlium ? Cilium’s toFQDN policies currently rely on a userspace DNS proxy to intercept responses and populate the endpoint's policy map. A userspace high availability mode for the proxy can avoid hard dependency on the agent at runtime. However this results in increased complexity and need for co-ordination between agent and out of process proxy.

So can we do better natively with eBPF ? Yes. This talk will explore how we can implement such a system and what it takes to integrate it into Cilium’s toFQDN policy sub-system.

abstract:

title: Sponsored Keynote: Breaking Up with Long-lived Secrets: Secure Automation in the Modern Age
abstract:
Previous attacks have shown that long lived tokens and passwords are an Achilles’ heel for software supply chains. When a secret tied to your build or deployment pipeline lives indefinitely, it becomes a high‑value target - leak it once and an attacker can wreak havoc undetected. Fortunately, there’s a growing shift toward authentication models that mint just‑in‑time credentials and retire them within minutes. These short‑lived, context‑bound tokens allow CI services, package publishers and signing tools to prove their identity without you as a developer needing to ever store long‑term secrets.

This talk introduces this emerging pattern and explains why it’s quickly becoming best practice for open‑source projects. We’ll look at how several ecosystems now let automated workflows access and publish packages using expiring tokens rather than hand‑entered passwords, and how this can be used in other applications like software signing. We'll talk about why moving away from long‑lived secrets dramatically reduces exposure, and show practical ideas for adopting short‑lived credentials in your own pipelines.

title: Introduction To Cluster API
abstract: Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) has emerged as the standard for declarative, GitOps-driven management of Kubernetes clusters. In this session, we will peel back the layers of the CAPI to reveal how its core controllers, webhooks and CRDs work together to reconcile your desired cluster state. You’ll discover how Machine and Infrastructure Providers translate high-level specifications into real infrastructure—whether on AWS, Azure, vSphere or even bare-metal. We’ll examine the mechanisms that enable automated cluster creation, scaling and rolling upgrades, and explore health-checking machines so that failures are detected and remediated automatically. By the end of the session, you will understand why Cluster API is far more than a collection of CRDs, and you will leave with concrete examples and code snippets ready to integrate into your CI/CD pipelines, empowering you to manage production-grade clusters with confidence and precision.

title: Sponsored Keynote: Unlocking GitOps at Intuit: Scalable, Reliable Environment Promotions
abstract:
At Intuit, managing over 20,000 applications, we ran into the same GitOps friction many teams face—scaling environment promotions often means turning off autosync and falling back on imperative pipelines, breaking the promise of Git as the source of truth.

As core maintainers of Argo, we tackled this by introducing a new set of GitOps Promotion Principles—supported by tools like the Argo CD Source Hydrator and the GitOps Promoter.
In this keynote, we’ll share how these innovations enable true GitOps at scale:

- Autosync stays ON
- Promotion history lives in Git
- Pull requests track promotion across environments

This approach is declarative, auditable, and automation-first—eliminating manual handoffs, restoring visibility, and giving developers confidence from commit to production. If you're struggling to scale GitOps, this talk offers a path to reliability and trust in every promotion.

title: Sponsored Keynote: Open Source Column Stores: The New Era of Observability Storage
abstract:
Observability has passed through several eras. It began with proprietary systems - powerful but closed and costly. The rise of search engines marked the next step, bringing more flexibility but exposing challenges of scale, cost, and performance. Specialized databases for metrics and traces followed, but instead of convergence, they introduced fragmentation—different engines for different signals, each with limitations that became clear at scale.

A new era is now emerging. Open source column stores such as ClickHouse unify logs, metrics, and traces in a single system, delivering the speed of real-time analytics with the efficiency of high compression and indexing. Integrated object storage enables virtually limitless retention without sacrificing performance, while open source foundations ensure flexibility and freedom from lock-in.

This talk will trace the evolution of observability storage, show why the fragmentation of the past is giving way to unification, and explain how column stores are redefining the future of scalable, cost-efficient, and open observability.

title: Sponsored Keynote: The Long Arc of Digital Rights: Securing our Open Source Future
abstract: Atlanta is the city that showed the world how principled, community-driven action can forge a more equitable future. The Open Source community is at its own inflection point, where our core principles of transparency, autonomy, and collective responsibility are being tested by new regulations like the CRA and the rapid evolution of technologies like AI. We can learn a lot from our history by leveraging critical principles to guide our response in today’s most urgent security challenges. Digital Sovereignty, an evolution of zero trust focused on autonomy, and the emergence of open source technologies like confidential computing and attestation are closer to making this a reality. As we navigate the complexities of the AI era and prepare for a post-quantum world with new cryptography, we must address critical gaps between technology implementation and the technologists available to do it. We can do this by reaffirming these principles through investment and collaboration to build a more secure and resilient open source ecosystem for everyone.

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Running Energy-Aware AI Inference on Edge Kubernetes With Kepler
abstract:
As AI workloads move to edge environments, it’s critical to balance performance with power consumption. In this lightning talk, we’ll demonstrate how to run a lightweight AI inference workload on a K3s-based edge Kubernetes cluster while measuring energy use in real-time — using only two core open-source tools.

The demo will deploy a simple ONNX Runtime-based image classifier and track its energy impact using Kepler (Kubernetes-based Efficient Power Level Exporter), with metrics collected by Prometheus. No GPUs, no complicated stacks — just a minimal, repeatable setup showing how even small inference jobs can be optimized for energy awareness. Ideal for platform engineers, AI ops, and edge developers interested in sustainable practices.

title: Sponsored Keynote: From Friction to Flow: Rethinking Observability for Developers
abstract:
Modern developers are expected to deliver resilient, secure, and high-performing applications at a pace that matches the speed of business. But the reality is often very different. Fragmented toolchains and traditional observability practices built for operation leave developers spending more time chasing issues than creating value. The result? Friction, frustration, and lost productivity.

This talk explores how observability must evolve to truly serve the developer experience. It’s not enough to collect logs, metrics, and traces; observability should empower developers where they work, in the moments they need it most. From IDE integrations to automated root cause analysis, to leveraging Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a new way of bringing observability data directly into AI-assisted workflows. Observability has the potential to shift from a reactive, operations-centric discipline into a proactive enabler of developer flow.

However, emerging neocloud providers, private GPU clouds, and bare metal clusters are becoming a core part of many organizations’ AI strategies as well.

In this session, one of the maintainers of vCluster reveals how they integrated Karpenter with tools like Terraform/OpenTofu, ClusterAPI (CAI), KubeVirt, and NVIDIA BCM to bring Kubernetes-native dynamic autoscaling to any environment and even allow for easy cloud bursting and hybrid cloud GPU clusters.

You’ll learn how this approach reduces idle GPU time, simplifies platform operations, and enables consistent AI infrastructure anywhere — from your own datacenter to neoclouds and hyperscale clouds alike.

Argo Rollouts is a Kubernetes controller for Progressive Delivery (blue/green and canary deployments). The controller already supports a plugin system for traffic providers (Istio, Traefik, Gateway API, etc.) and for metric providers (Prometheus, Datadog, etc.). In the latest release, the Argo team completed the trilogy by implementing support for Canary Step plugins. This extends Argo Rollouts capabilities and enriches the progressive delivery experience to accommodate a multitude of scenarios.

With Canary step plugins, you can now fully control what happens DURING the canary process and implement any custom functionality that you want within the canary steps. Did you always want to do canary gating? Deployment sync between different controllers? Custom notifications while the canary is running? Now you can!

In this talk we will see the architecture of the new plugin mechanism and explain how you can extend canary deployments with your own custom workflows.

title: What the Diff?
abstract:
Have you ever run into the situation where Argo CD does not recognize that a change to a resource has occurred? What about when resources report being out of sync unexpectedly?

"What the diff!?!?" (or some other more colorful expression).

Argo CD features a robust diffing system for determining whether resources within Kubernetes clusters match their declared state. Most users experience the same three way diff used by Kubernetes which relies on comparing live state, desired state and the last-applied-configuration annotation However, this just scratches the surface for how Argo CD compares resources.

In this session, attendees will explore the wide world of diff’ing in Argo CD; the different strategies, exclusion methods, common pitfalls, and techniques. By using scenario-based examples from real world Argo CD use, attendees will not only master a foundational concept in Argo CD, but apply their learning within their own environments.

Go from “What the diff” to “thats the diff”!

title: IPv6 First, Not Just Ready: Kubernetes Without IPv4 Using Cilium at ESnet
abstract:
ESnet, the U.S. Department of Energy’s high-performance research network, runs Kubernetes on-prem in IPv6 only network using Cilium as our CNI. While Kubernetes introduced IPv6 support in version 1.22, deploying production grade clusters without IPv4 presents unique challenges that require careful architectural design such as:

- Support for DNS64, NAT64 in the underlying network
- Obtaining a stable egress IPv6 address
- Traffic patterns (ingress vs. egress)
- To masquerade or not to
- Allocating PodCIDR, ServiceCIDR sizes correctly
- Choosing between tunneling vs. native routing mode and it's implications

Attendees will learn how we solved these problems using Cilium features such as:

- eBPF datapath using kube proxy replacement
- BGP, load balancer IPAM, GatewayAPI
- NAT46x64Gateway in absence of NAT64 gateway on the network

We will also discuss steps to deploy an IPv6 only KIND cluster using Cilium and how that can be useful for testing applications during development.

title: You Got a Match! LLM Prefix Aware Routing With Kubernetes
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are revolutionizing industries, but serving them efficiently and cost-effectively on Kubernetes presents challenges. Diverse prompts and request patterns can lead to poor GPU use, higher latency, and rising costs. This session explores prefix-aware routing—a method to intelligently route, prioritize, and cache LLM inference requests in Kubernetes. By analyzing the initial tokens (“prefix”) of incoming prompts, the system identifies patterns and optimizes accordingly. This allows reuse of cached data (like KV caches), improved batching of similar requests, and efficient use of model shards or LoRA adapters. We’ll examine the architecture of a prefix-aware scorer plugin, its integration with the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension, and real-world performance benefits. Learn how this approach boosts throughput, cuts latency, and maximizes resource efficiency for GenAI workloads running on CNCF infrastructure using smarter routing strategies.

title: From Squire To Network Knight: Defending the Kubernetes Castle the Cloud Native Way
abstract:
In medieval times, a squire was the first step toward becoming a knight. In Kubernetes, many of us start the same way eager to protect our clusters, but armed with the wrong tools and assumptions. In this talk, we’ll start with a wide-open Kubernetes cluster — no policies, no protections — and walk through what’s missing, why it matters, and how to build security the cloud native way.

We’ll contrast static, perimeter-based firewalls with Kubernetes native policy and show how to evolve from static IPs to identity-based enforcement. Step by step, we’ll build protections using Network Policies and Cilium’s identity-aware, DNS-enforcing, and observability-rich capabilities.

Along the way, you’ll learn to debug common issues, avoid the traps of “firewall thinking,” and think in terms of intent, not infrastructure. By the end, you’ll have the tools and mindset to go from squire to network knight.

You'll follow a connection's complete journey: observing data as it traverses filter chains, understanding the interactions between filter types, and revealing what truly happens when Envoy processes network traffic. Beyond the technical details, you'll gain valuable engineering insights into how Envoy's threading model and memory management techniques enables both high performance and extensibility. You'll leave with practical insights into Envoy's inner workings, empowering you to troubleshoot, enhance, and customize Envoy to suit your organization’s needs.

title: From Edge To Insight: Cybersecurity Intelligence With Kubeflow, VLLM, and GraphRAG
abstract: As threats evolve across cloud and edge surfaces, modern cybersecurity demands adaptive, policy-aware AI systems that can detect, reason, and respond autonomously. In this session, we present a security-centric, federated architecture built on Kubeflow. Lightweight ONNX models run on K3s-based edge clusters to analyze Falco logs and detect anomalies locally, minimizing exposure. Only filtered signals and key features are shared to uphold compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and zero trust principles. In the cloud, KubeFlow orchestrates a GraphRAG pipeline powered by vLLM and Knowledge Graph reasoning aligned to NIST and MITRE ATT&CK. This architecture supports detection, intelligent recommendations and rule automation—such as policy and rule updates—deployable back to the edge. Designed for high-stakes environments like healthcare, OT, and critical infrastructure, this session equips security and DevSecOps teams with practical tools to implement self-improving, compliance-aligned AI defenses.

title: Breaking the Latency Barrier: Tackling Compute and Network Delay With Globally Distributed Wasm
abstract:
Latency isn’t just a backend problem or a network issue—it’s both. Reducing time-to-response means optimizing not only how far your workloads have to travel (network latency) but also how fast they spin up and execute once they arrive (compute latency). Solving one without the other leaves users waiting.
This talk introduces Spin, the open source developer toolkit that uses WebAssembly (Wasm) to reduce compute latency to near-zero. With sub-millisecond cold starts and scale-to-zero efficiency, Spin apps can be built in a local dev loop and then deployed anywhere with no changes to the code. That same application can be deployed to any SpinKube cluster or globally across Akamai’s 4,000+ edge locations. The result is serverless applications that feel instant, no matter where users are.

title: How UW Madison Monitors 25+ Clusters With Cilium and Prometheus Agent on a Student-Sized Budget
abstract: Budgets keep shrinking while observability demands explode—so how do you capture L7 insight across 25+ Kubernetes clusters without paying a sidecar tax? At UW Madison, we paired Cilium’s eBPF networking with the Prometheus Agent’s remote write, streaming rich flow telemetry to a central Grafana stack at a fraction of the usual footprint. Live on stage, we’ll fire test traffic with curl from a single app pod and watch Cilium Flow Metrics spike and Alertmanager light up within seconds—no sidecars, no context switching. You’ll leave with a field-tested playbook: scrape-target pruning, discovery patterns that survive air-gapped research zones, and the real story of what broke first—and how we fixed it. title: Telemetry That Matches Your Model, Verified Live
abstract:
OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions define how telemetry should look, but do instrumentations actually follow them in practice? Your organization might define additional conventions - but how do you ensure instrumentations stay up to date as conventions evolve?

What if you could get a comprehensive report on the actual telemetry your application produces, checked against your conventions model?

We’re excited to share OpenTelemetry Weaver’s live check: a validation tool that listens to telemetry in real time and analyzes its compatibility against formally defined conventions. We’ll show you how to run live checks in your CI/CD pipelines to catch instrumentation issues before they hit production - no more guessing whether your telemetry matches your model.

Beyond basic model compliance, we’ll also demonstrate how to write Rego policies to enforce organization-specific checks and best practices.

title: From Adoption to Innovation: LinkedIn’s SPIRE Journey
abstract:
You may already be familiar with SPIFFE and SPIRE—CNCF projects that provide secure, cryptographic identities for workloads. At LinkedIn, we've adopted SPIRE as a foundational component of our identity infrastructure, operating at massive scale to issue certificates for hundreds of thousands of hosts and workloads across on-premises clusters in production.

While SPIFFE and SPIRE are important building blocks for a Zero Trust architecture, they cannot be directly applied to meet LinkedIn’s unique requirements. In this talk, we’ll share how we addressed key gaps by leveraging OSS SPIRE’s extensibility, along with additional components we developed, to meet LinkedIn’s security requirements and handle the scale and complexity of our ecosystem. This includes establishing a hardware-based root of trust across varied hardware, securely bootstrapping Kubernetes clusters from bare metal to applications, enabling agentless workload attestation and certificate issuance, and so on.

title: How Secure Is Academic Open Source? Insights From the UC OSPO Network
abstract:
Academic institutions produce a large amount open source software, especially in scientific research, but security is often not a priority. Many academic developers lack training in secure practices, so widely used tools can remain vulnerable or poorly maintained. University OSPOs work to close these gaps by promoting sustainability and better practices. However, measuring project health and security at scale remains a major challenge.

This talk shares a University of California (UC) wide effort to build a dataset of UC-affiliated GitHub projects and assess their security and health using tools like OpenSSF Scorecards, static analysis, contributor centralization, and dependency analysis. We’ll present preliminary findings, discuss challenges unique to academic software, and propose a reproducible method other universities can adopt. Our work reveals tooling limitations and opportunities for OSPOs to better support researchers, fostering safer, more sustainable academic open source.

title: Spice Check: Building an E2E SLSA Implementation - Adolfo García Veytia, Carabiner Systems
abstract:
Significant work has been invested in the SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) specification and the tools that generate the unforgeable evidence necessary to protect software. And for a while, the only missing part was a way to enforce those protections.

Now, we are ready to lock tight our software factories 🚀

With the recent release of the AMPEL policy engine and the SLSA 1.2 spec that includes the SLSA Source track, we can now write policies to harden software repositories and builds at each step from source to release. All based on signed, verifiable evidence.

This talk will showcase the new SLSA 1.2 spec, diving into the new source track as we protect a software release by enforcing policies at each stage of the SDLC with attested data from various tools.

We will describe how to leverage the AMPEL policy engine and through the collection of policies curated by its community we will instrument end to end protection for a software project with almost no code.

abstract:

During this talk, we will share insights from pilot organisations and uncover some of the more common pitfalls.

Adopt the Platform Maturity Assessment and begin benchmarking your platform maturity today!

title: There Is No Silver Bullet: The Complexities of Building IDPs
abstract:
The allure of an internal developer platform (IDP) is tantalizing, isn't it? You've watched the talks, and you know why having one would make life better for yourself, your team, and your customers. However, using a handful of open-source software (OSS) or Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects in your organization a magic silver bullet.

When building an IDP, a lot factors come into play.

* Do you set up a centralized approach for syncing configurations across dozens of clusters?
* Is a service mesh truly necessary?
* How can make the most of shared clusters while not becoming the system-admin keeping everything together.
* How do you expose services internally and externally in a way that prevents disjoint dev teams from introducing network misconfigurations?

This talk won't prescribe solutions. Instead, it will draw on experiences from building platforms at Viasat; highlighting often missed considerations for those just starting their platform-building journey.

title: Beyond Review Apps: Orchestrating Full-Stack Ephemeral Environments with Argo CD
abstract:
Traditional review apps often fall short when testing complex multi-service interactions. At SeatGeek, shared staging resources made this a massive pain and prevented true isolation. We solved this by building "Ephie" – an ephemeral environment capability using Argo CD that empowers engineers to create fully isolated, multi-service environments on demand.

Unlike traditional review apps, Ephie spins up complete application stacks with configurable isolation for databases, message queues, and interconnected services. A custom Kubernetes operator dynamically generates Argo CD Applications for each service and shared resource, scaling to support thousands of ephemeral environments.

Attendees will learn the architectural patterns we used for custom operators managing Argo CD Applications, resource isolation strategies using a service mesh, and how this unlocked previously impossible testing capabilities, transforming development workflows.

title: Server-Side Diff: Future-Proofing ArgoCD's Comparison Engine
abstract: This talk will deep-dive into the new Argo CD feature called Server-Side Diff as it provides a crucial architectural shift that leverages Kubernetes Server-Side Apply moving the diff computation away from Argo CD. We'll explore the reasons why this paradigm shift was not just beneficial but necessary for modern GitOps at scale. You'll gain insight into the technical details of how the feature works, enabling teams to achieve reliable previews of what their operations will actually accomplish. This means catching potential problems during the diff phase, before any changes are applied, drastically reducing the risk of failures. Learn how this innovation future-proofs Argo CD for robust, enterprise-scale GitOps environments. We'll share invaluable lessons learned from building and scaling this critical functionality, offering practical takeaways that you can apply to your own applications and infrastructure. Join us to discover how to achieve truly reliable and predictable GitOps.

title: Containing Wildfires in a Sprawling Multi-Cluster Network: The Network's Immune System
abstract:
In a sprawling multi-cluster network, a security breach in one pod is never just a local problem. It’s the potential start of a wildfire. The real danger isn’t the initial compromise, it's the attacker's lateral movement across clusters, turning a small incident into a catastrophic failure.

Traditional incident response is too slow; by the time a human can analyze logs and apply new firewall rules, the damage is done. How can we build a system that detects a threat and automatically "shrink-wraps" the blast radius in real-time?

This session presents a cutting-edge, automated threat containment system built on the combined power of Cilium, Tetragon, and Hubble. We demonstrate a closed-loop workflow that transforms your network from a passive conduit into an active immune system.

Join us for a live-fire demo where we’ll compromise a service and watch the mesh quarantine the breach, proving you can contain wildfires before they rage out of control.

title: This Lying Has To Stop: Keeping AI Honest with OpenTelemetry
abstract:
Building an automated engineering journal sounds straightforward enough. Git commits provide facts, AI adds intelligent context, and you get queryable documentation about the history of your project without manual work. Except in development, the AI assistant lies. Confidently.

When debugging breaks down because your AI assistant hallucinates, OpenTelemetry provides the observability needed to understand what actually happened versus what your AI claimed happened.

The session follows Commit Story, an AI-augmented engineering journal, through authentic debugging disasters, using live demos to show how these lies could have been caught sooner. This talk will explore traces of commit-triggered AI calls, teach techniques to verify response trustworthiness, and share guardrails that help prevent AI deception in the first place.

abstract:

Step 2: Deploy them on Kubernetes
Step 3: Profit (less hassle, more automation)

This session will introduce AI agents, programs that use LLMs, interact with tools, retrieve data, and communicate with other agents. We will cover what agents are, why you might need one, and how to build a Kubernetes-native agent using CNCF tools such as Kagent. We’ll also explore emerging protocols like MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent to Agent), and share how the CNCF’s Working Group on AI (WG-AI) is working to build guidelines and publish whitepapers on security, sustainability and agents in this space.

Whether you're new to Kubernetes, AI, or both, this talk bridges the gap between AI concepts and practical cloud native implementations, giving you the foundational knowledge to start building autonomous cloud-native AI applications.

title: Rethinking the Proxy Model: Implementing Envoy as a Node-Scoped Agent
abstract:
Sidecar proxies are the most common paradigm for service mesh deployments in Kubernetes, but we're going to explore a radical alternative: deploying Envoy as a node-level proxy instead of a per-pod sidecar.

We'll delve into the motivations for this shift, examining how moving the data plane to the node level addresses the concerns with sidecar deployments. We will also dive deep into the core technical changes in Envoy to make this possible.

The talk will also cover the critical aspect of configuration management in this new model. We'll illustrate how service mesh configurations are represented and applied in a node-level Envoy deployment, contrasting it with the familiar sidecar model.

Finally, we'll present comprehensive resource usage and performance comparisons, demonstrating the tangible benefits in terms of reduced memory footprint, lower CPU consumption, and improved overall throughput that can be achieved by consolidating Envoy instances at the node level.

title: Streamline LLM Fine-tuning on Kubernetes With Kubeflow LLM Trainer
abstract:
Fine-tuning LLMs on Kubernetes is challenging for data scientists due to the complex Kubernetes configurations, diverse fine-tuning techniques, and different distributed strategies like data and model-parallelism. It’s crucial to hide complex infrastructure configurations from users, and allow them to gracefully shift among diverse fine-tuning techniques and distributed strategies.

This talk will introduce Kubeflow LLM Trainer, a tool that leverages pre-configured blueprints and flexible configuration overrides to streamline the LLM fine-tuning lifecycle on Kubernetes. The speaker will demonstrate how Kubeflow LLM Trainer integrates with multiple fine-tuning techniques and distributed strategies, while offering a simple yet flexible Python API. Attendees will see how LLMs can be fine-tuned on Kubernetes with just a single line of code, highlighting how Kubeflow LLM Trainer streamlines, simplifies, and scales LLM fine-tuning on Kubernetes.

title: Dirty Dancing - Untrustworthy SLSA Build Provenance
abstract:
Achieving SLSA Build Level 3 is often seen as the gold standard for building trusted software. Projects across CNCF and the broader open source community proudly declare they've reached this milestone but, what does that actually prove?

This talk breaks down what SLSA Level 3 really means, using the official slsa-github-generator workflow as a case study. We’ll examine how provenance is generated, what’s verified (and what isn’t), then walk through examples where provenance can appear valid but should not be trusted.

We’ll explore how subtle gaps in build tooling, configuration, or verification can undermine trust, and offer practical guidance on:
- Comparing other builders to the official SLSA tooling
- Identifying red flags in provenance attestations
- Using SLSA tools correctly to ensure real trust

It’s a reality check for consumers and maintainers alike, helping them understand not all provenance is created equal.

title: We're All Consumers (And That's Dandy)
abstract:
The OpenSSF Baseline aims to simplify and standardize the collection of security control and compliance information from open source projects. Like nutrition labels, much of the Baseline contents are derived from international legislation. If you maintain open source software, unfunded “compliance frameworks” probably sound like a drag.

While you might be right, the silver lining from this cloud might just be bigger than the shadow. In this talk, I'll show you four ways that Baseline can make your project better and maybe even save you some pain and heartache down the line. Because everyone building open source is also a consumer of open source, and Baseline aims to provide a nutrition label for the open source you consume.

These organizations will eventually discover that they can advance each of the aspects of their platform maturity (referencing the CNCF Platform Engineering Maturity Model) by including expertise already available with UI/UX Design and Application Engineering teams in the platform development process.

In this talk, UI/UX Design and Software/Platform Engineering professionals will present learnings from both platform customer and platform developer perspectives to help organizations understand the value of including design from the start, in cloud native platform development.

abstract:

But we all know that endless consumption is harmful, and that we need to curb it fast. But how? States and Companies pledge on this, routinely missing deadline after deadline. Capitalism … grumble … capitalism.

But what if, Capitalism was the answer? What if we can leverage our company’s need to reduce its cloud bill also to reduce our power consumption?

In this talk, Ramiro and Nancy will talk about how platform teams are key actors on this, and how we can leverage ARM, Kubernetes, observability, and autoscaling technologies to build a culture of true on-demand infrastructure that not only reduces our cloud bill but might help save the world.

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Rate Limiting With Quotas Is Hard - So We Didn't!
abstract:
At Tesco, the UK’s biggest supermarket, we run Envoy as a distributed API gateway configured with a purpose-built xDS control plane. We wanted to apply rate limits globally and prototyped a server that implemented Envoy’s RLQS (Rate Limit Quota Service) - a protocol where quotas are distributed dynamically. But API traffic distribution shifts constantly across our Envoy fleet, and we had issues with accuracy as our quota allocation updates lagged behind changes in traffic distribution.

This talk will cover the problems we faced and our evolving design choices as we went from a prototype to a low-overhead and accurate distributed rate limiting solution running in production. During this journey we broke away from RLQS and designed and implemented an alternative protocol that allows us to maintain rate limiting accuracy in the face of rapid traffic redistribution, without extra latency. It also means we need to process orders of magnitude less data in our central rate limiting service!

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Streamlining MLOps Pipeline With Kubeflow on Arm64 Locally
abstract: Can you run KubeFlow in a box, and do useful things with it? That is the challenge we posed ourselves as we tried to apply the qualities of KubeFlow - its composability, modularity, scalability, and portability – in a constrained physical compute footprint. We present here a case study of using KubeFlow on a single host, with up to 192 CPU cores, to deploy and run AI pipelines with KubeFlow Pipelines, and to serve workloads like LLMs with KServe. We will measure the performance across a range of workloads, and show that it is possible to meet SLOs for advanced AI workloads like agentic AI without large GPUs or access to cloud services.

abstract:
Most platform engineers are stuck in the same loop: too many tools, too little time, and no clear path forward. Supporting developers while keeping infrastructure stable and scalable is no small task, but the right open source projects can help.
In this session, we’ll take a look at Backstage, KubeVela, Argo, Flux, Dapr and Crossplane and see how they work in practice to simplify infrastructure management, enable GitOps workflows, improve developer self-service, and bring order to complex environments.
Think of it as your shortcut past weeks of trial-and-error, minus the late-night Slack threads. You’ll walk away with a battle-tested toolkit and ideas you can actually use Monday morning.

title: Securing the Edge: Multi-Cluster Governance With Kyverno on K0rdent’s Fleets
abstract:
As organizations scale AI workloads and applications across edge environments, enforcing consistent governance and security policies becomes increasingly challenging. This session introduces a practical approach to scalable policy enforcement across fleets of Kubernetes clusters using Kyverno and k0rdent, with k0s as the lightweight Kubernetes distribution powering edge nodes.
The session covers fleet-wide governance strategies, including dynamic resource allocation (DRA) for GPUs, policy automation in disconnected or constrained environments, and real-world patterns for enforcing compliance in the field.
Through demos and architecture walk-throughs, this session provides actionable insights for those deploying Kubernetes at the edge, particularly in industries like telco, manufacturing, and smart infrastructure. We will also share patterns for integrating policy-as-code workflows and automating Kyverno validation via CI/CD or offline pipelines.

title: Panel: AI Infra Best Practices: Enterprise Do’s and Don’ts
abstract:
Kubernetes has emerged as the de facto platform for training, serving, and batch workloads. Traditionally, Enterprise Readiness for Kubernetes involved logging, monitoring, analytics, security, and multi-tenancy considerations. Do AI workloads present new and/or unique enterprise readiness requirements?

Does high cost and limited availability of hardware accelerators like GPUs present new challenges?
Should you plan silo stacks for pre-training, post-training, serving, and batch? Or can you consolidate multiple stacks on a single cluster?
Should you plan for a large number of small clusters or a small number of large clusters?
Should you stick to a single region/cloud or federate across regions/hyperscalers/neoclouds?

This panel aims to share wisdom from:
- Power Users with long running AI deployments
- Builders of modern Kubernetes-based AI frameworks like Ray powering training, serving, and batch use cases
- Practitioners onboarding heterogenous AI use cases for enterprise users

title: Taming the Wild West of Research Computing: How Policies Saved Us a Thousand Headaches
abstract:
When you let researchers loose on your Kubernetes clusters, it doesn’t take long before the whole place turns into the Wild West: interactive GPU pods left running for days, large CPU-only jobs stampeding onto GPU nodes, and resources vanishing like water in the desert. So we did what any good admin team would: we brought in the sheriffs - Kyverno, Kueue, and Argo CD - to lay down the law and bring order to the frontier.

In this talk, we’ll share how we used these tools to enforce fine-grained policies, implement fair-share GPU scheduling, and automate governance across our Accelerated Discovery bare-metal clusters. No custom code, no cowboy hacks - just smart policy design and GitOps discipline.

Whether you’re managing research workloads or just trying to keep your clusters from descending into chaos, this session will show you how policy-as-code can save you a thousand headaches - and maybe a few GPUs too.

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Beyond Lua: Lightweight Envoy Extension With JavaScript
abstract:
With the introduction of dynamic modules in Envoy, it becomes much easier to write high performance custom extensions for Envoy using languages other than C++, which opens up a whole new world of possibilities for Envoy users.
However, the dynamic modules feature itself is low-level and requires a good understanding of Envoy's internals,
especially it must be written in C, C++, Rust or other compiled languages that can be compiled to a shared library.
On the other hand, in practice, platform developers might not be familiar with these languages.

We developed a JavaScript extension built on top of the dynamic modules feature, which allows users to load JavaScript code as an HTTP filter. This is a powerful example of how to use the dynamic modules feature to create high-level extensions in a more accessible language.

In this lightning talk, I will quickly review the dynamic modules feature, and then introduce the JavaScript dynamic module we developed with a live demo.

abstract:
As AI development accelerates, platform engineers must keep up with rapid changes in LLMs, model infrastructure and deployment practices. Meanwhile, developers expect intuitive, self-service access to the latest tools, while still maintaining governance & standardization.

In this talk, we’ll share our journey using Software Templates to support AI workflows in a fast-changing environment. We’ll cover practical challenges we faced, including:
- Keeping pace with frequent LLM updates and evolving model architectures
- Automating GitOps and infra updates using tools like Renovate
- Bridging the gap between template UX expectations and current Backstage capabilities

We’ll also walk through how we built and maintained templates, integrated with Tekton, ArgoCD, Model Catalog to support AI development at scale. Whether you're a platform engineer, AI practitioner or contributor, you’ll leave with real-world lessons & actionable insights for using Backstage in evolving software ecosystems.

This new capability allows users to run distributed Spark workloads directly from their notebooks, making it easier to move from data exploration and feature engineering to model training and serving, all within a unified platform.
In this session, we will demonstrate how users can launch notebooks with a Spark kernel and run analytical workloads through the Spark Operator. title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Taming the BPF LRU: Eliminating TCP Resets in Cilium - Gyu Tae Bae, NAVER Corp.
abstract:
At scale, Cilium users often face mysterious TCP connection failures from unexpected RST packets. This session explores a critical bug where Cilium's BPF-based SNAT and its LRU eviction policy prematurely terminate active sessions. We will dissect the root cause in the eBPF datapath and reveal the elegant fix, now merged upstream in Pull Request #37747: proactively restoring the original NAT entry on the reverse traffic path. This solution, born from a real-world production issue, reduced connection failures from up to 10% to nearly zero.

This talk is a must for operators debugging network instability and developers tackling real-world eBPF challenges. You will leave with a clear diagnosis for this "silent killer" and key insights into building robust, high-performance cloud networking.

abstract:
Kubernetes has become the de-facto standard to deploy and operate containerized applications. But understanding Kubernetes can be difficult or time-consuming.

Several years ago I asked myself how I imagined the concepts of Kubernetes: a pod, a deployment, a service, a secret, a configmap, a cronjob… and then I created a new way of explaining Cloud technologies.

In the first part of the talk, I will tell you a story, I will tell you my story. How, during more than two years, I worked every evening/nights/week-end to explain Kubernetes in sketchnotes, in blog posts, videos and finally published everything (and more) in an illustrated book of more than 270 pages (with all the concepts included Debugging / Troubleshooting and Tips) and why I continue to do it.

And in the second part, I will explain Kubernetes concepts to you ... in a visual way :-).

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: Service Quality Management for Critical Edge Applications
abstract:
Edge applications require high-computing power and low latency responses, while running on resource-constrained devices. Maintaining consistent, high-level service performance is challenging in heterogeneous and dynamic edge computing conditions (server load, network traffic, jitter, etc.). In that situation it is very difficult to ensure stable edge service quality.

We propose an open-source solution that monitors the entire edge chain (applications, UE, network, servers with Kubernetes), analyze the correlated data, plan a service quality action and execute the plan.

The solution has been fully developed and tested with a small set of real-world use cases.

title: Rendered Manifests and OCI
abstract:
GitOps principles aim to tackle visibility and collaboration challenges in Kubernetes, emphasizing a declarative desired state and continuous reconciliation. Configuration tools like Helm and Kustomize streamline manifest management in GitOps but introduce a dilemma; these abstractions are central to GitOps, but having Argo CD mutate them at runtime obscure the actual impact on deployed manifests. This led the way to the Rendered Manifests pattern (also known as Hydration), which aims to remove the obfuscation and provide an immutable source of truth.

But how does this pattern work with OCI? With the addition of OCI in Argo CD v3.1, users can now use OCI to store manifests. How does that impact the Rendered Manifests pattern? In this talk Christian will go over some patterns with OCI and rendered manifests, what works, what doesn’t work, and what to look out for when adopting OCI in your Rendered Manifests workflows.

title: The Case for ArgoCD and CdEvents Integration
abstract:
Today’s complex, distributed CI and CD ecosystems, tools often operate in silos, making it challenging to achieve true interoperability & end-to-end observability. Introducing cdEvents, a CDF spec that standardizes how tools across the Application Delivery domain can communicate. Explore why common events are crucial for modern distributed CI and CD, enabling automated workflows, unified observability, & seamless tool integration.

We’ll share how cdEvents transforms isolated deployment notifications into a common language that spans the entire App Delivery domain. We'll examine how ArgoCD could support cdEvents, from leveraging existing notification systems to emitting standardized deployment & incident events. Finally, the benefits of integration: enhanced pipeline automation, vendor-neutral observability, simplified tool migration, & the ability to correlate ArgoCD with upstream CI events & downstream ops incidents. Come understand why a future of cdEvents & ArgoCD should exist.

abstract:

Managing large fleets, ensuring config stability, controlling costs, and maintaining data quality are complex hurdles not covered in tutorials. These issues hinder the reliability of observability platforms and engineering velocity.

This panel unites operators from Capital One, Liatrio, and OllyGarden to share hard-won experience. We'll discuss their strategies for managing collector fleets, ensuring safe rollouts, handling problematic data like long traces, and the path to a stable Collector v1, sharing real-world lessons from the trenches.

Rather than one prescriptive solution, attendees will hear a dynamic discussion. They will learn diverse strategies for tackling stability, cost, and fleet management from operators in the trenches. This panel offers a chance to learn from the shared experiences and differing opinions of experts, empowering informed decisions.

title: Panel: Balancing Developer Freedom and Security
abstract:
Kubernetes and containers turned out to be great for developer freedom -- they could quickly build containers running the software needed with their preferred tooling, and it would run happily next to a container running a completely different stack. But unless care is taken, this flexibility comes at a cost; a proliferation of containers, all running different base images and different software. Or the same software but at different versions. Or the same versions but with different base images and extra dependencies. Along with this proliferation comes the perils of CVEs from out-of-date or bloated software.

So what can you do to get this under control? Come listen to a panel of speakers who have seen this before and learned how to deal with the problem.

abstract:
Can we secure AI workloads, agents, and MCP servers the same way we secure traditional microservices? Are established tools and standards—such as SPIFFE identities, mutual TLS, authorization policies, and supply chain security—sufficient, or do AI workloads require a fundamentally different approach?

This panel discusses the unique challenges AI introduces across multiple dimensions: model selection, enterprise operations, hardening and red teaming, end-user management, model compute optimization, and long-running, context-heavy sessions. We’ll also explore disaster scenarios such as multi-cluster/region failovers, and what they mean for securing distributed AI applications.

Join our panel of AI and security experts for a dynamic discussion that clarifies what can be reused and what must be reimagined to effectively protect AI workloads.

abstract:

Landmark legislation like the EU’s Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) or the US’s NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) bring software engineering practices into clearer focus and shine the light of global regulation into the darker corners of how modern software is crafted.

Join this panel of Compliance-enthusiasts, as we speak about these movements using the lens of the upstream open source maintainer. We will discuss the opportunities and challenges facing open source maintainers and showcase the OpenSSF’s Security Baseline and associated tools. Attendees will learn the value of implementing the Baseline to help reduce the noise from downstream asking projects to comply with “regulation de jure” in this globally-connected development world.

title: Panel: Navigating Promotions: Insights From the Argo Community
abstract: The 2025 Argo CD Survey highlighted key frustrations in promotion workflows: limited visibility, manual processes, challenges establishing and standardizing quality gates, and difficulty maintaining consistency at scale, with nearly 67% of users relying on DIY solutions like scripts and in-house tools. title: Panel: What They Don’t Tell You About Shipping Argo CD V3.0: A Maintainer’s Panel
abstract:
Argo CD v3.0 marks the first major release since 2021 and a major turning point for the project. But behind every milestone is a story: design debates, roadmap disagreements, community wins, painful PRs, and lots (and lots) of learning.

This panel brings together core Argo CD maintainers who will share what it takes to ship a major release like v3.0 and maintain it. We’ll go through the motivations behind this release, dive into how architectural decisions are made (and challenged), what motivated the big changes in v3.0, how we handle governance, promote contributors, and resolve conflict, whether it’s over code, community norms, or contributor expectations

Lastly, we’ll also share some very real human moments: PRs we instantly regretted, design threads that got heated, and the awkward but necessary conversations that help projects (and people) grow. This session is for anyone curious about what happens behind the Git history and how Open Source really works beyond the changelogs.

This centralized platform has revolutionized the way our development teams interact with tools, services, and resources, leading to substantial improvements in efficiency and innovation.

Ericsson’s DX journey exemplifies the transformative power of a portal based on Spotify's Backstage platform, in driving efficiency, innovation, and business success. We have harnessed automation, standardization, and collaboration to empower our teams and accelerate delivery by reducing cognitive load and streamlining workflows, as we create an environment where developers can thrive.

title: Fit-to-Serve: How a New DRA Capability for Dynamic Device Sharing Fits Into Distributed LLM Serving
abstract:
llm-d is a community-driven effort to modernize large language models serving at scale—natively within Kubernetes. The core is modular architecture that decouples prefill and decode operations. This disaggregated design unlocks precise tuning of computing and network resources, tailored to the unique demands of each phase.

But here’s the twist: how precise can it be defined? A GPU unit? A MIG slice? Maybe even something finer? With a new capability proposed for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) framework, resource capacities for compute and network devices can now be dynamically requested and adjusted on the fly. At the same time, the core DRA capability enables device selection based on fine-grained attributes—including topology awareness—eliminating the need for clunky hacks or rigid resource pools.

In this talk, we will demonstrate how a new capability of DRA makes the llm-d framework more feasible and cost-effective, explore the remaining challenges, share practical insights.

title: Life of a Mobile Span
abstract:
Molly isn't like the other spans from the Land of OTel. Like her friend Spanley, Molly writes everything down—but for different reasons. You see, the events in Molly’s life are unlike any that other spans see. That's because she lives outside the center of the city of Data.

Molly looks forward to that day when she can tell her own story in full. To friends. To parents she's never met. To the world. Because she has a world-changing secret no one knows.

Inspired by a talk that Jamie Danielson and Yuri Oliveira Sa gave at OTel Community Day, this will be the story of a span recorded on a mobile app told in a narrative form.

Find out how different life is for spans outside the data center, part technical, part whimsy. Learn about how runtime factors in mobile make accepted notions about modelling, semantic conventions, and delivery different, where the conventions and spec of OTel make things challenging, but also creates new possibilities that make observability unique on mobile.

title: 🧙‍♂️ Abracadabra! OTTL Turns Profiling Into Metrics
abstract:
What if you could conjure real-time insights from profiling data—no storage spells required?
In this session, we’ll explore how the OpenTelemetry Transform Language (OTTL) works like a wizard’s spellbook, letting you transform raw profiling data into actionable metrics on the fly. Using the collector-ebpf-profiler as your Marauder’s Map, you’ll learn how to enable profiling in Kubernetes and channel that data through a second collector for real-time processing.
We’ll demonstrate how to cast powerful OTTL transformations, measure resource usage during live profiling, and unlock the magic of this emerging observability signal—without ever writing to disk.
No enchanted memory bowls—just pure, live telemetry sorcery.
