title: Driving Policy To Secure the Open Source Ecosystem
abstract: The Log4shell vulnerability and the XZ Utils compromise drew global attention to the security of open source software. How did policymakers respond, and what does the future of OSS security look like? In this talk, former CISA senior advisor Jack Cable will detail his experiences leading open source software security efforts at CISA and writing the first U.S. legislation on open source software security in the Senate. Perhaps unsurprisingly, policymakers can be quick to propose actions that can counter the ethos of the open source community. Jack will walk through past, present, and future work to secure the OSS ecosystem and how you can get involved.

title: It's Not a Best Practice If No One Can Follow It: Learning From Our Container Security Mistakes
abstract:
Ten years ago, container security was complex, fragmented, and hard to operationalize. Both Twistlock and Alpine Linux were early efforts to help teams harden their containers – Twistlock by detecting and alerting on risks, enforcing runtime protection, and enabling container-level microsegmentation; Alpine by providing minimal, hardened base images. But neither fully solved the problem. Twistlock’s approach was powerful but not always easy – most teams didn’t know where to start, and writing practical segmentation policies was notoriously hard. Alpine, while popular, often broke builds, lacked key language support, and left teams maintaining security-critical patches on their own.

In this talk, John Morello, CTO of Twistlock and now co-founder of Minimus, and Alex Zenla, CTO and co-founder of Edera, will share what they’ve learned – and today’s engineering teams can apply those lessons to hardening their own container deployments.

title: SAFE-MCP: A Security Framework for AI+MCP (Model Context Protocol)
abstract:
Introducing SAFE-MCP, a comprehensive security framework for Model Context Protocol (MCP) - the emerging standard for AI tool integration.

Based on real-world security research from 2024-2025, SAFE-MCP maps 65 attack techniques across 14 tactics (at time of writing), providing defenders with actionable intelligence to secure AI systems. This talk reveals how attackers exploit MCP through techniques like Tool Poisoning (where hidden instructions in tool descriptions compromise AI behavior), Command Injection (affecting 43% of MCP servers, per Equixly), and novel attacks like MCP Rug Pull.

Drawing from incidents at major organizations and research by organizations like Invariant Labs, Equixly, and Backslash Security, we'll demonstrate practical detection and mitigation strategies. Attendees will learn to identify vulnerabilities in their AI deployments, implement security controls, and contribute to this community-driven framework.

title: Building PCI Compliant Kubernetes Platforms - Demystified, Fun, and Possible
abstract:
Imagine building a secure, scalable platform as your organization's backbone—meeting PCI compliance while optimizing for efficiency. Let's explore crafting such a platform using self-managed Kubernetes, with lessons learned, a blueprint for technologies and practices that you can apply to your own environment.
GitOps and Zero Trust are our guiding principles. ArgoCD helps us automate, ensure consistency, and deliver traceable, auditable changes, enabling speed without compromising stability.
To manage Kubernetes' self-hosted complexity, we leverage tools like Crossplane and Cluster API (CAPI), enabling declarative management of clusters and resources with SDLC best practices that align workflows with PCI standards. We balance responsibilities between platform engineering and tenants, fostering collaboration and ease of use without sacrificing security. Join us and explore this path to a compliant, efficient, and trusted platform – it is possible to enjoy compliance!

title: From Duct Tape To Declarative: Playtika's Platform Overhaul at Unicorn Scale
abstract:
Success is a double-edged sword. As the gaming industry boomed, Playtika’s platform couldn't keep pace. What was once manageable became chaos: Ansible scripts, imperative Jenkins pipelines, a sprawl of internal portals & everyone doing automation their own way.

Environments took days to spin up.
Onboarding was guesswork.
DON'T touch the fragile parts.

This talk unpacks how Playtika modernized that mess into a CNCF-driven platform stack. Learn how they moved to declarative K8s clusters with ClusterAPI, GitOps deployments with FluxCD, and infra managed via Crossplane. Internal tools were replaced with a single Backstage-powered portal, delivering developer efficiency at scale.

But the real shift wasn’t just technical—it was cultural.

Ticket ops became self-service. Teams aligned. Provisioning dropped from days to under an hour all with OSS.

If your platform feels like it’s held together with duct tape and hope, this talk shows how standardization isn’t boring—it’s what scales.

title: Blazing-Fast Container Deployments: Image Caching With Block Storage
abstract: In the fast-paced world of Kubernetes, deploying containerized workloads—especially AI/ML models—demands speed and efficiency. Traditional container image pulls from remote registries often bottleneck deployment times, particularly for large, complex images. This session introduces an innovative solution: caching base container images using remote block storage to significantly enhance deployment times and boost cluster efficiency. We’ll delve into how block storage serves as a backing store to cache container images across all nodes in a Kubernetes cluster. Attendees will explore the architecture, implementation steps, and real-world performance gains from our production deployment for NVIDIA Cloud Functions, showcasing a remarkable 52%+ reduction in deployment times. Whether you’re managing AI-driven microservices or latency-sensitive applications, this session equips you with practical strategies to accelerate your Kubernetes deployments using cutting-edge storage solutions.

title: Is Your Service Mesh AI Ready?
abstract:
AI workloads look like traditional micro-services in many ways: they run a variety of workloads, connected over the network, and require security, observability, and traffic management. Exactly what Istio does! So, can Istio solve all of our AI infrastructure problems? Not so fast.

While sharing some similarities with traditional workloads, AI brings a number of new requirements onto the infrastructure to effectively manage and control.

In this talk, I will cover the new problems AI workloads bring, and where Istio fits in, including what Istio can manage today, what is on the roadmap, and what is left out of scope. We will cover optimized inference load balancing, LLM protocol awareness, and more.

This talk aims to highlight pain points where the real complexity begins while building features using OpenFeature in a multi-cluster, multi-cloud environment managed by open source k0rdent
We'll explore how platform engineers can manage feature lifecycle across the Kubernetes multiverse, from progressive rollouts to flag-based experimentation using OpenFeature as the control layer and k0rdent as the policy, observability, and automation backbone. We’ll emphasise on designing GitOps-friendly feature flag workflows using OpenFeature and enforce policy-driven feature rollout gates with k0rdent.

Come observe flag impact across clusters using k0rdent’s telemetry and enable safe, self-service feature toggling for developers in distributed teams.

title: Does the Component Model Require Extra Copying?
abstract: The WebAssembly Component Model enables cross-language interoperability, automatic safe bindings generation and lightweight sandboxing based on the Component Model's Interface Definition Language, WIT, and its underlying "shared-nothing" memory model. However, hearing "shared-nothing" often raises the question of whether these benefits come at the cost of runtime overhead due to additional copying. This talk will explain how, using the existing and planned features of 0.2, 0.3 and 1.0, developers can avoid unnecessary copies in most if not all performance-sensitive scenarios, preserving the performance of "rolling your own ABI" without the heavy engineering lift.

abstract:

Stefan will then discuss the current state of GitOps practices and the latest developments of Flux Operator around the Open Container Initiative (OCI), where OCI Artifacts are becoming the de facto standard for distributing the desired state of Kubernetes clusters and applications.

Finally, Stefan will share his thoughts on the future of GitOps in the context of Agentic AI. He will showcase the new Flux MCP Server, a tool that connects AI assistants to Kubernetes clusters, and discuss the security implications of using AI in production.

abstract:
CI/CD pipelines are the lifeblood of modern software delivery yet for many teams, their performance and reliability remain opaque. While production observability is mature, visibility into the CI/CD journey before code reaches production is often missing.

In this session, we introduce a new frontier: CI/CD observability powered by OpenTelemetry, with a deep dive into Argo Workflows and ArgoCD. With the latest CI/CD Semantic Conventions in OpenTelemetry, teams can now generate standardized, vendor-neutral telemetry from their GitOps-based delivery processes.

We’ll show how to:

Instrument Argo Workflows and ArgoCD with OpenTelemetry to generate traces and metrics.

Capture critical signals across build, deploy, and promotion stages using OTel's CI/CD semantic model.

Whether you're running large-scale delivery platforms or just getting started with Argo, this session will equip you with practical insights to bring your pipeline observability out of the dark.

title: Managing Millions of Storage Volumes at Scale: Inside DigitalOcean's ArgoCD Strategy
abstract:
When you're managing millions of storage volumes across 13 regions, traditional deployment approaches break down. At DigitalOcean, we transformed our Storage Platform operations using ArgoCD to bring sanity to complexity.

In this talk, we'll share how DigitalOcean's Storage Platform team turned our deployment process into a GitOps-powered engine using ArgoCD. We'll take you behind the scenes of operating our Storage Kubernetes platform, StorK8s, our storage orchestration platform that powers millions of volumes across DigitalOcean's global infrastructure.

You’ll learn:

1. How we architected a single ArgoCD instance to manage 13+ clusters across 13 regions while maintaining sub-5-minute deployment times.
2. Real-world canary and blue-green deployment patterns for stateful workloads.
3. Why centralised GitOps beats federation for our use case (and when you shouldn't follow our lead)

We’ll share what worked, what didn’t, and secret ingredients that helped us scale GitOps reliably.

This session focuses on the self service template that deploys MCP servers and a Backstage plugin that displays these servers in the Backstage Catalog, including their tools, and monitors approval statuses, providing centralized governance and visibility. Attendees will learn how this approach standardizes AI infrastructure deployment, enhances collaboration, and ensures compliance. This case study offers practical insights into operationalizing AI workflows with CNCF tools and Backstage, benefiting organizations integrating AI into their cloud native ecosystems.

We'll dive into the latest challenges in deploying and scaling large language models (LLMs) — including inference performance, KV-cache management, distributed execution, and cost optimization.

Attendees will gain insights into the technologies powering the next wave of AI applications and learn how to prepare their infrastructure for a generative AI future.

title: Scaling Pain Points in the World of Observability!
abstract:
Observability is essential—but scaling it often reveals deeper issues than it resolves. As organizations grow, telemetry gets fragmented across tools—metrics in one place, logs in another, traces somewhere else—making it hard to correlate data when it matters most. The result? Missed alerts, unclear root causes, and degraded customer trust.

These aren’t just tooling problems—they’re collaboration problems. Developers end up searching for signals instead of solving real issues, draining productivity and slowing delivery. In this talk, we’ll explore common observability scaling challenges—from dashboard noise to onboarding friction—and the hidden costs they carry for teams and the business. We’ll also look at how open standards like OpenTelemetry can help, and where gaps still remain.

You’ll leave with practical insights, community-sourced lessons, and a clearer path toward building observability that empowers rather than overwhelms.

title: OSCAL in Action: Real World Examples of Automating Policy & Compliance
abstract:
Imagine you're trying to read a book while someone's simultaneously ripping out pages, rewriting chapters, and gluing in new sections. That's what gathering compliance evidence in a cloud native environment is like. The rapid evolution in how systems are deployed, secured, and governed leaves organizations struggling to connect abstract cybersecurity regulations with concrete, enforceable policies.
This talk provides a practical blueprint for bridging that gap. We'll show how CNCF projects - like the newly released OSCAL Compass Compliance-to-Policy (C2P) v2 and Open Policy Agent (OPA) - work together to transform regulatory requirements (expressed in Open Security Controls Assessment Language) into actionable policy-as-code artifacts that generate verifiable, audit-ready evidence. Focusing on the end-to-end approach, we'll dive into the tools and practices involved, providing real-world examples of automating compliance in cloud-native environments.

title: Securing Cloud-Native Workloads from the Metal Up
abstract:
Kubernetes is the standard for running workloads now, whether in public cloud or in a datacenter. With costs of public cloud increasing, many companies are now considering repatriation of expensive workloads on-prem.

Running on-prem with actual physical servers that are racked, stacked and cabled is exciting, and can be cost-effective; however, it's a different security model that requires much more planning than spinning up a VM in your favorite public cloud provider.

We will explore how to secure workloads on bare-metal, by rooting our trust in TPMs onboard physical servers. We will introduce SPIRE and SPIFFE; then dive into how your applications can chain their identities back to the hardware on which they run, illustrating the power of hardware-backed security for cloud-native workloads. We will also briefly cover vTPM offerings from cloud providers, and discuss how you can implement a common machine-identity backed architecture whether in the cloud or in the datacenter.

title: What Doesn’t Kill You Makes You Stronger: The Vulnerabilities That Redefined Kubernetes Security
abstract:
A decade ago runC escape CVE-2019-5736 proved a single process could seize an entire node. Five years later, CRI-O’s cr8escape showed the threat hadn’t gone away, it just moved. We’ll sprint through five pivotal CVEs that rewrote Kubernetes threat models and examine how these vulnerabilities were discovered, exploited, mitigated and we’ll uncover patterns and lessons that have shaped the security landscape.
Instead of a history lesson, we’ll decode each incident into a reusable threat-model pattern and will describe what capability was abused, which boundary failed, and which control closed the gap. Alongside the controls that were built into Kubernetes, we’ll spotlight the open-source tools that each crisis propelled into the cloud-native landscape and explain why operators still rely on them today.
Attendees will gain insight into how the security of containerized workloads has matured and explore the shifts within the ecosystem that have driven today’s increased resilience.

title: Kubernetes-Powered Platform Engineering: From IaC To API-Driven Infrastructure
abstract: Discover how leveraging Kubernetes for platform engineering can dramatically increase development efficiency, streamline operations, and enable unprecedented scale through Kubernetes-native GitOps. This session explores how the Kubernetes API becomes the cornerstone of GitOps practices, solving key challenges in managing cloud resources and infrastructure at scale. Learn how this Kubernetes-centric approach transforms traditional workflows, allowing teams to declaratively manage thousands of resources across complex environments using familiar Kubernetes objects and methodologies. We'll demonstrate how platform abstractions help overcome complex challenges, and how automation aligns with Kubernetes controllers principles using open-source tools. Explore how the powerful combination of Kro, ArgoCD, and ACK extends the Kubernetes API to drive GitOps for both applications and infrastructure, revolutionizing platform engineering on EKS through a truly Kubernetes-native GitOps approach.

abstract:
Scaling modern systems is hard—fragmentation, cognitive overload, and operational risk grow fast. At Spotify, we build and operate Portal, our Backstage-based Internal Developer Platform for external customers. But here’s the twist: we use Portal to run Portal. By dogfooding our own platform and tapping into Spotify’s internal observability and tooling ecosystem, we deliver faster, smarter, and with more joy—for both our teams and our customers.

In this talk, Andrew Sail (Lead for Backstage/Portal Platform Engineering & SRE) and Laurén Roshore (Lead for Spotify’s internal Observability & Monitoring platforms) share how building with the same tools we provide sharpens empathy, reduces MTTR, and enables richer, more scalable defaults. You’ll learn how internal-external partnerships help us accelerate delivery and operate with confidence. This is a talk for anyone building platforms who wants fewer fire drills, better feedback loops, and happier engineers at every layer.

title: YAML Is My DBA Now: Our Postgres Journey From DIY To Autopilot Self-Service
abstract:
They told us, “Don’t run databases on Kubernetes.” We heard, “Challenge accepted.” This is the story of how we went from handcrafted Postgres chaos to a stable, CNCF-aligned DBaaS using CloudNativePG over the years — and lived to tell the tale.
We started with containers, then pinned nodes in Kubernetes (spoiler: not scalable). Zalando’s operator with Patroni got us partway, but the real leap came with CloudNativePG: rebuilt from scratch, capable of autopilot.
You’ll hear real incidents (yes, including “the one with the wrong PVC”), lessons learned, and how we’ve moved from tickets to self-service via GitOps. So what happens when YAML becomes your new DBA?
This is a story of maturity, simplicity, real benefits CNCF brings to your project. Not just from a single project, but from the whole ecosystem evolving over the years in networking, deployment, and much more.
Whether you're building a platform or escaping vendor lock-in, come laugh, learn, and reconsider running DBs in Kubernetes.

abstract:
Kubernetes and GitOps are now industry standards, but adopting these at scale in a regulated, large multinational enterprise environment poses many architectural challenges and compliance requirements to solve for (especially in production). With thousands of engineers whose familiarity with Kubernetes and Cloud Native technologies like Flux and Helm vary widely, platform teams need to account for ways to upskill the engineering community, streamline developer experience, and reduce the time to delivery.

In this session, we will discuss how we built a platform (powered by Flux for application workloads) that allows for automated tenant GitOps workflow onboarding, enables app teams to deploy to multi-cloud targets, and enforces least privileges and multi-tenancy.

We will also discuss how we leverage Buckets as the source store for Flux Kustomizations and enhance Flux custom metrics with Prometheus and Kube State Metrics, subsequently surfaced in Grafana dashboards.

title: Istio Ambient Goes Multicluster
abstract:
Running multiple clusters boosts reliability, infrastructure diversity, and fault isolation but introduces security, configuration, and networking challenges. Istio ambient multicluster aims to connect these clusters with the same security, control, and observability as single-cluster ambient.

This talk will showcase our alpha implementation of Istio ambient multicluster, compare it with Istio sidecar multicluster, and discuss cross-cluster encryption, security policy enforcement, service discovery, traffic control, and observability. We'll also cover our compromises and future roadmap.

Attendees will gain the knowledge and familiarity to try out ambient multicluster, provide feedback, and assess adoption feasibility.

title: AI Ships Fast and Breaks Things — Feature Flags Keep It Controlled
abstract:
AI agents and AI-powered IDEs are reshaping how code is written, tested, and shipped, but our deployment infrastructure isn’t ready. Traditional CI/CD pipelines assume a sequential flow of change. With AI in the loop, change becomes concurrent, agent-driven, and continuous. Developers are shifting from authorship to orchestration, managing a dynamic system of AI contributors. To keep this complexity safe and observable, we need a new kind of control plane, and feature flags sit at the center of it.

This talk explores how feature flags are emerging as the interface between AI and production. They provide a flexible, auditable control layer that matches the pace of AI-led development. You’ll learn how agents can write code with flags embedded, how OpenFeature enables vendor-neutral flag integration, and how telemetry-aware AI systems can manage flags autonomously. In an AI-driven world, feature flags aren’t optional; they’re essential.

title: Curating OpenTofu Modules & Patterns
abstract:
It's often too easy to informally share IaC source. At scale, this practice may lead to dependencies on unmaintained code. To address this, we’ve introduced standards for sharing of modules and patterns to give users transparency on module usage, maintenance and function. Transparency is achieved through a maturity rating, applied to each module and curated by the IaC Platform team.

Through collaboration with module authors and a custom Backstage plugin for module discovery, we enable teams to filter modules by a range of categories, making it easier to find and use reliable modules. Beyond individual modules, we provide module implementations of larger architecture patterns to accelerate delivery.

In this talk will share our approach to managing module sprawl, applying standards and building a culture of inner-source collaboration to ensure sustainable and effective use of Tofu at scale.

title: Whamm: A Framework for Performant, Sandboxed Instrumentation.
abstract:
Wasm workloads are often black boxes in terms of observability, but insight into their execution is mission-critical. Where are the hot paths? How resource-heavy is the workload (e.g. usage metering)? What cache strategy is best? Does the program follow our security policies?

This talk presents Whamm, an instrumentation framework that can be used to answer questions like these. Whamm can statically rewrite bytecode ***or*** dynamically insert probes via an engine interface to invoke callbacks at runtime. Whamm’s engine interface promotes portable instrumentation with high-performance. This is achieved through leveraging engine optimizations that reduce overhead and providing logic as Wasm code, which the engine can compile and/or inline into application code. Whamm supports instrumenting Wasm modules, components…and even kernel-level events! Want to know how? This session offers an overview of the framework and a live demo of writing monitors, helping you apply Whamm in your domain.

abstract:

In the opening of the keynote, he’ll deliver key project updates, highlighting recent achievements and offering a glimpse of what’s on the roadmap.

Flux’s adoption is evolving from a deployment engine into a governance control tower for software delivery, ensuring compliance, security, and trust across environments. Andy will bring his perspective on how teams in regulated industries, including major banks, use Flux to embed policy and auditability directly into their workflows, shifting from manual operations to continuous governance by design. 

Andy will also introduce the vision behind Flux’s MCP, laying the foundation for AI-assisted GitOps. This will bring even greater clarity and control to complex systems and configurations. As part of this, Andy will reference the AI reference architecture and plans to evolve Flux MCP.

Finally, there will be a moment to celebrate the growing ecosystem, from core maintainers to contributors at GitLab, Microsoft, and projects like Headlamp, to many others helping drive Flux forward. title: Sponsored Keynote: Stretching the Limits of S3 Backend for OpenTofu
abstract:
What if we could have all the benefits of a managed state backend (like Terraform Cloud) but on top of a state bucket as-is, without requiring any additional storage or other moving parts beyond a simple stateless API? How far can we stretch it?

Turns out, surprisingly far. Yes S3 is not fast; but neither is HCL - most of the time it spends waiting for provider-initiated requests. So storage is rarely the bottleneck.

This talk will show you that achieving some of the advanced managed state backend features on top of an S3 state bucket with state files is actually not that hard. Specifically:

- remote backend API proxy
- versioning
- rollbacks
- cross-state dependency tracking
- Authentication compatible with the `cloud` block
- Role-based Access Controls (RBAC)

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: AIxCC Results and New Open Source AI Projects To Help Secure Open Source Software
abstract:
The Artificial Intelligence Cyber Challenge (AIxCC), led by DARPA in collaboration with ARPA-H, aims to secure open source software through AI.

AIxCC competitors have developed AI systems to automatically find and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities in open source software used in critical public infrastructure.

OpenSSF's role as a challenge advisor to the AIxCC is to ensure the competition provides solutions that benefit open source culture and community. At the conclusion of the challenge, the systems from winning competitors will be open sourced. The infrastructure and data from the competition will also be released as open source to support ongoing research efforts.

This presentation will provide an overview of AIxCC, including the results of the finals competition from Def Con in August 2025 and how the systems performed. It will also cover OpenSSF’s support for the process of releasing this research as open source software following the conclusion of the finals event.

title: CANCELED ⚡Lightning Talk: Unveiling Hidden Risks: Vulnerabilities in Shared Kernel Isolation on Kubernetes
abstract: Containers look isolated, but in Kubernetes, they all share the same Linux kernel. That shared surface means even obscure kernel bugs can crash nodes or impact other workloads. This talk shows real examples from ext4, io_uring, userfaultfd, configfs, and tracefs, where unprivileged containers triggered kernel panics and data loss. These issues had no CVEs and little visibility. Attendees will learn why shared kernel isolation is risky and why Kubernetes security must include kernel awareness.

title: ⚡Lightning Talk: AI at the Edge: ONNX Inference in WASM on Featherweight K0s
abstract:
This session explores deploying ONNX machine learning models via WebAssembly on lightweight k0s Kubernetes clusters—enabling fast, secure AI inference in resource-constrained environments. The talk demonstrates running pre-trained models from frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow through ONNX, executed inside WebAssembly’s sandboxed runtime on minimal Kubernetes.

Topics include:
– ONNX Runtime with WebAssembly on k0s
– Using WASI to access and run models
– Optimizing performance for Wasm-based inference
– Model loading, caching, and scaling strategies
– CI/CD integration for Wasm ML pipelines

Attendees will see real-world benchmarks comparing Wasm-based vs. containerized inference, focusing on latency, memory usage, cold start, and throughput. This approach reduces infrastructure cost, improves isolation, and unlocks edge AI use cases where traditional containers fall short.

title: Fix Production Rollouts on the Fly With Agentic AIOps
abstract:
Your software rollouts to production are probably always flawless, right? For the rest of us, once in a while we do run into issues when releasing code to production. Argo Rollouts is a great tool to help mitigate these issues by progressively delivering software to production, and automatically rolling back new features if anything doesn’t go right.

Wouldn’t it be nice if we can take this functionality to the next level? We can take advantage of the advances made in Agentic AI and instruct a model to analyze the logs when a rollout fails. Then thanks to the use of agents, it can take action on our behalf, such as fixing the code or the deployment manifests on the fly, creating new PRs and sending notifications. The sky is really the limit.

Come to this session to learn how to combine Argo Rollouts with Agentic AI to achieve the most seamless release experience yet.

title: Revolutionizing Argo Integration With Model Context Protocol: An AI-Driven Approach
abstract: This presentation introduces an innovative approach to developing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for the Argo project suite within the CNOE Platform Engineering AI Assistant framework. We demonstrate an automated, AI-powered solution that generates MCP servers for Argo CD, Workflows, and Rollouts. Beyond simple OpenAPI conversion, our method leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance API context and descriptions. The solution features automated maintenance through GitHub Actions, enabling Argo maintainers to effortlessly keep their APIs updated. This low-touch approach represents a significant advancement in AI agent plugin frameworks, specifically tailored for CNCF tool integration. At CISCO we are using this process to generate MCP servers for Argo for our internal developer platform Assistant Jarvis.

This "messy middle" stage often creates technical silos, leaving engineers drowning in operational overhead. While scaleups eventually need dedicated platform teams, how do you effectively start one? This talk is a case study of how Backstage becomes the perfect bootstrapping solution, delivering quick wins that justify platform team investment. You'll learn how to standardize technology choices with composable templates and improve observability via catalog-driven automation. You'll get battle-tested strategies for using Backstage to build the foundation and business case for your first platform team, transforming chaotic environments into organized, scalable engineering organizations.

title: Wasm't That Easy: Securing MCP With Wasm Sandboxes
abstract:
Running third-party MCP servers is a bit of a wild west. Who wants to download yet another random binary, cross their fingers, and hope it behaves? We want tools that are sandboxed by default, with an explicit, auditable policy for what they can access. This is the problem the WebAssembly (Wasm) Component Model excels at.

We'll show you how we're using Wasm Components to make AI Agents safer. We’ll ditch insecure runtimes and heavy containers for lightweight, sandboxed binaries with deny-by-default permissions. This approach gives us fine-grained control: no more unwanted file access or calls to untrusted domains.

Through live demos, we’ll tackle the real risks: from untrusted code sneaking into your supply chain to malicious tools exfiltrating your data. You'll see us pull a tool from an OCI registry, block it from accessing system resources, and prevent data exfiltration attacks in real-time. Join us to learn how you can build and shape a more secure AI ecosystem.

title: Envoy Filters: Powering Effortless Observability at Scale
abstract:
At Pinterest, a scalable, low-friction way to improve observability and track service reliability is desired. Our solution is to leverage Envoy proxy filters. In this talk, we will introduce how we developed the Envoy ZooKeeper proxy filter that processes 250K requests per second across more than 100 ensembles—enabling real-time metrics, reliability tracking, and operational visibility without disrupting critical infrastructure, such as modifying service code or redeploying services.

This approach generalizes to both L4 and L7 protocols—including gRPC and Thrift—and showcases how Envoy filters can serve as a powerful observability tool in high-scale, production environments.

title: There's a Lot of Bad Telemetry Out There
abstract:
Much telemetry is bad: noisy, costly, and hides real signals. Auto-instrumentation can create high-cardinality floods, while over-instrumentation results in excessively verbose traces with countless near-useless internal spans. These common issues obscure insights and strain collection pipelines, leading to frustration and wasted resources.

This session dissects these "bad telemetry" patterns using real-world examples (like verbose traces and auto-instrumentation noise at global scale). We'll demonstrate concrete fixes both at the source, and using OpenTelemetry Collector configurations—like filter, attributes, span, and transform processors—to tame this data at the pipeline level, improving quality and utility.

Attendees will learn to identify bad telemetry, apply OTel best practices to create, filter, and reshape data, and cultivate higher-quality, cost-effective, actionable insights.

title: Escape Plan: How We Survived Without EKS and Learned To Love Air-Gapped
abstract: Running Kubernetes in the cloud is convenient—until you need to run it where the cloud can’t follow. This talk tells the story of how we migrated our production SaaS platform from Amazon EKS to a fully air-gapped environment. It wasn’t a lift-and-shift. We had to replace everything from identity management and observability to networking, secrets, and storage—without the crutches of managed services. We’ll share what broke, what surprised us, and how we rebuilt key platform functions using open source, cloud-native tools that don’t depend on AWS. We’ll dive into our biggest wins and regrets, how we kept the developer experience intact, and why this move ended up making our platform more secure, resilient, and portable. If you’re building platforms for restricted, regulated, or disconnected environments-or just want to design for freedom instead of lock-in-this session is packed with practical lessons and honest takeaways.

title: Let the Platform Build Itself: Using AI To Construct an Internal Developer Platform With CNCF Tools
abstract:
What if you could build your Internal Developer Platform (IDP) by simply describing what you want and let AI do the rest?

In this talk, we'll explore how large language models, agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers can be used not just to operate an IDP, but to build one from scratch. We'll demonstrate how AI systems can reason about infrastructure needs, policies, workflows, and developer experience patterns to compose a fully operational IDP using CNCF projects, such as Crossplane, Backstage, Argo CD, Kyverno, and others.

All of this will be shown in a live demo where an AI system, guided by natural language input and assisted by MCP servers, constructs a functioning platform in real time.

Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of how AI tooling can accelerate platform engineering, reduce cognitive load, and shift the role of humans from builders to architects of intent.

title: Why Data Stored in Kubernetes Is at Risk and What You Can Do About It
abstract:
As more teams run databases, AI pipelines, and other stateful workloads on Kubernetes, persistent storage has become one of the most important and most overlooked parts of cluster security. Snapshots, backups, and volume mounts often go unprotected, even though they contain the data your business depends on.

This session takes a clear look at how to secure Kubernetes storage in production environments. You'll learn how to use CSI driver features like encryption, mount options, and identity-aware access, how to monitor and audit usage with tools like Falco and Kubescape, and how to protect snapshots and backups from common threats like ransomware and insider risk.

Whether you're running Postgres in production, building ML pipelines, or just adding persistent volumes to your apps, this talk will give you a practical checklist to strengthen your storage layer without adding unnecessary complexity.

abstract:

In this talk, we’ll explore how feature toggles, typically used to launch features, can be just as powerful for retiring them.

We’ll cover real-world examples and lessons learned from within Octopus and discuss tips on how feature toggles help you clean up your codebase without fear. If your product roadmap is filled with more "we should remove that someday" than you're comfortable admitting, this talk is for you.

abstract:
Flux Unfiltered lifts the curtain on the people, pivots, and production issues behind CNCF Flux’s rise from a Weaveworks side-project to a graduated GitOps staple now stewarded by ControlPlane. After recording 8+ hours of candid interviews with founders, maintainers, cloud providers, telcos, banks, and platform vendors, we distilled four recurring themes:

-Why GitOps emerged (and when it doesn’t fit)

-How regulated industries tame Kubernetes drift with Flux

-What happens when commercial backing disappears—and how the CNCF kept the project alive

-Design trade-offs that differentiate Flux and Argo today

In this session we’ll share the insights and findings from the docu-series—surface actionable patterns for teams adopting GitOps at scale. No sales pitch, no product demo—just hard-won lessons and a roadmap of where the community is steering Flux next.

title: Multi-messenger Security: Adaptive Kubernetes SOC From Disparate eBPF Tools
abstract:
The linux kernel through eBPF offers to unify the disparate fields security and observability through shared data structures. We show how a K8s Security Operations Center, organically composed of established eBPF projects (CNCF Kubescape, Pixie and Tetragon) can see signals that the individuals cannot.

We explain how we achieve both a comprehensive baseline and use independent signals to dial up/down coverage as suspicious indicators surface. The mutual independence of signals from across processes, file system, and network activity achieves a high signal-to-noise, enabling manageable data volumes and facilitating selective forensic storage.

You will see a *live demo of the io_uring root-kit which is hard to detect for sys-call based security tools in their default configurations, however almost trivial to detect with our adaptive setup.

Additionally, our SOC architecture is node-local, and no data leaves the cluster meaning you remain sovereign and in control of your data.

title: OSPS Baseline: Improving Your Project Security the Easy Way
abstract:
No developer wants to ship deliberately insecure code. At the same time, security is often not their expertise and security improvements often seem like an unfunded mandate from extractive corporations. “I’m not a supplier” is a common refrain. Nevertheless, improving a project’s security posture helps the entire ecosystem, including the overworked maintainer. The Open Source Project Security (OSPS) Baseline gives maintainers clear, actionable guidance on security policies at a level appropriate to the project’s size.

In this talk, attendees will learn how to apply the OSPS Baseline to their project, how OSPS Baseline differs from similar projects like OpenSSF Scorecard, and why adopting OSPS Baseline in their project helps them and their users. Maintainers with compliance obligations (like for the CRA) will learn how OSPS Baseline can simplify meeting their compliance requirements.

title: The Whole Is Greater Than the Sum of Its Parts: A Case for Interoperable Supply Chain Tooling
abstract:
Development related to software supply chain security has been tremendous in the last few years: From foundational projects like in-toto and DSSE, to the Sigstore and SLSA projects, to new entrants like Minder and GUAC.

While these frameworks can work well by themselves, their full potential is revealed in their combination. However, tooling interoperability is not always seamless: an organization's supply chain includes upstream suppliers and downstream users, who may choose different tooling. Even when organizations seek consolidated tools like Sigstore with in-toto, each still uses different methods to store signature information, encode data at rest, etc.

What would it take to make these tools work well together?

In this talk we’ll discuss gaps, show example approaches to fill them, and remaining work for better tooling interoperability. The audience will leave with a deeper understanding of these technologies and how to use them together to improve their supply chain security.

abstract:

This talk covers the integration of KitOps and Argo Workflows, which streamlines the process from development to production. KitOps a CNCF Sandbox project simplifies packaging models into immutable, attestable units with full traceability, while Argo provides K8s-native orchestration for deploying these models securely and reliably.

For ML engineers and DevOps teams alike, this integration reduces friction between model creation and deployment, improves compliance through verifiable artifacts. We’ll walk through real-world pipelines that showcase how to securely package & deploy models in a reproducible manner. Also learn how to eliminate configuration drift with GitOps-driven enforcement and embed security checks into ML-specific CI/CD.

By the end, attendees will gain a clear understanding of how to build production-grade ML pipelines without compromising on security.

abstract:

We tackled this by migrating 2,000+ ArgoCD Applications across six regions and 11 environments to a centralized ApplicationSet-based platform. You’ll learn how we secured business support to prioritize this tech debt—framing it as a developer productivity investment—and how we built a culture of GitOps ownership across 200+ developers.

Our AppSet repo enabled team-specific patterns, auto-discovery, easy promotions, and self-service—all while reducing sync times and failure rates. But the real win? A mindset shift: platform became enablers, not gatekeepers.

If you're looking to scale GitOps while empowering teams and getting executive buy-in, this session will leave you with the tooling, structure, and organizational playbook to make it happen.

title: On-Call the Easy Way With Agents
abstract:
Debugging an API traffic system over a service mesh like Istio is complex and time consuming. By building out integrations with data plane observability sources such as Splunk and Wavefront, creating RAGs over internal documentation and platform-specific information, and implementing runbook steps like kubectl or istioctl commands as tools, you can create an Agent AI that can perform existing on-call tasks and react to situations. Using alert descriptions and common debugging results as input, this agent can analyze what the issue is, identify the next debugging or remediation steps to take, and even perform those steps.
At Intuit, the Mesh Debug Deputy was created to do exactly this, and provide significantly reduced time to resolve alerts and a streamlined on-call experience. It can respond to Pagerduty alerts, gather information from Splunk, Wavefront, and internal data sources, perform additional debugging and data gathering, and finally run real commands to actually fix issues.

abstract:

While they are useful they are far from completing the triage experience. At eBay's Observability team, we have been hard at work trying to concoct the apt explainer that can explain time series. Through the crafty use of traditional machine learning techniques coupled with next generation LLM goodness, we are enabling time series explainers in order to provide our SREs a CoPilot that will help triage issues much faster. This talk explains:

* what the challenges are in explaining time series
* techniques applied to engineer the explainer
* candidate use cases that are being enabled as a CoPilot to provide assistance during triage
* other explainers that provide an edge during triage
* future work that this unlocks

This talk is a continuation of our journey in leveraging AI in reshaping observability.

title: High-Volume Logging Without High Cost: Flight Recorder for OpenTelemetry Logs
abstract:
Organizations face escalating costs from high-volume application logs—most never used. In response, teams aggressively filter logs, risking incident blind spots.
This talk introduces the Flight Recorder pattern for OTel Logs: instead of continuously exporting logs via OTLP, applications export them to ring buffers—ideally backed by OS-native mechanisms like Windows ETW or Linux Tracepoints, but also implementable in user space. Logs remain local, continuously overwritten until triggers—critical errors or operator requests—cause buffered logs to be exported via OTLP to OTel Collector, maintaining existing workflows.
Once triggered, the system also enters a temporary streaming mode, exporting all new logs continuously for a brief period. This approach eliminates unnecessary logging costs while ensuring logs are readily available when it matters. We’ll present a design and working prototype that shows how this model delivers substantial cost savings without sacrificing observability.
session_types: Observability Day/Managing the Ever-increasing Volume of Observability Data

In this session, we’ll dive into how Kyverno enables declarative governance and automation across environments without complex admission webhooks or YAML gymnastics when paired with k0rdent, a multi-cluster container platform built for distributed Kubernetes operations.

We’ll walk through real-world use cases where Kyverno and k0rdent combine to power secure developer self-service, enforce platform standards, support AI/ML workloads, and reduce operational toil. This is platform engineering done right, resilient by default, policy-driven by design, and open source at its core.

title: The Cost of Apache Kafka
abstract: Strimzi makes it easy to run Apache Kafka on Kubernetes. But persistent volumes and high-throughput cross-zone traffic can quietly become major cost drivers. In this talk, we’ll show how you can use OpenCost and NetObserve to build an open source, cost-aware view of our Kafka infrastructure — and how we tuned it to be leaner and smarter. While OpenCost doesn’t track network costs out of the box, we’ll show how to extend it with NetObserve data to estimate cross-zone network costs, attributing them directly to the pods generating the traffic. OpenCost can also help us to monitor compute and storage costs. We’ll share an open-source-driven playbook for cost-effective Apache Kafka on Kubernetes, informed by real-world experience and actionable strategies, without relying on proprietary tools or commercial observability platforms.

title: Building the Next Gen GitOps-based Platform With ConfigHub
abstract:
Managing Kubernetes configurations at scale inevitably leads to what we call "config hell" - a maze of interconnected Helm charts, Kustomize overlays, and FluxCD manifests that become increasingly difficult to understand, debug, and maintain. Teams spend countless hours troubleshooting why a change in one environment didn't propagate correctly to another, or why a seemingly simple configuration update broke an unrelated service three clusters away.
Consider a real scenario we faced: A routine patch required updating a ConfigMap across 30 instances of Grafana in as many clusters, in 6 environments. What should have been a 10-minute change turned into a 3-day investigation when services started failing in seemingly random patterns. The root cause? Helm template logic interacting with ConfigMap did not take into account spaces in between dashboard names. The configuration files looked correct in Git, but the rendered manifests told a different story.

title: Optimizing Istio Autoscaling: From Resource-Centric To Connection-Aware
abstract:
Scaling Ingress Gateways in a service mesh is deceptively tricky. Traditional metrics like CPU or request throughput often fall short, especially when applications handle long-lived connections like GraphQL, WebSockets, or streaming APIs.These workloads can appear idle to the HPA,even when they’re operating near connection saturation.
In this talk,we’ll share practical insights from operating a multi-cluster Istio mesh and walkthrough how we improved the autoscaling of Ingress Gateways by shifting from resource-centric to connection-aware scaling.We’ll discuss how we modeled traffic using active connection count,to make the HPA work as required. You’ll also hear how we tuned node sizing & pod resource limits to eliminate cold starts and avoid bin-packing issues.
If you’re running Istio in production and want to avoid 503s for cross cluster,scale smartly,& control cost-all while respecting the nature of long-lived connections-this session offers hands-on learnings you can adopt today.

title: From “What Broke?” To “What Changed?”: Unlocking Feature Flag Observability
abstract:
Imagine your monitoring dashboards are flashing red. Error rates are through the roof and your team has spent an hour digging into the code trying to identify the problem. You are still trying to find WHY knowing remediation is still steps away.

This talk is for teams using feature flags for releases, A/B tests, and permissions in modern codebases. We'll demonstrate best practices to reduce Mean Time to Recovery by adding feature flag observability to your workflow. Using the OpenTelemetry Demo, we'll show how feature flags can become a key part of your observability platform, helping you quickly see the impact of changes, not just what broke. The result: instant remediation instead of an all-hands-on-deck emergency.

Learn about the new OpenTelemetry feature flag semantic convention that can be the step towards improving your feature flag observability and find what changed instead of what broke. Sometimes the best root cause analysis is the one you do after the fire is out.

title: How OpenTofu Uses LSP To Power Its Text Editors Plugins
abstract: The integration of Language Server Protocol (LSP) with OpenTofu empowers text editor plugins with robust Infrastructure as Code (IaC) capabilities. LSP provides a standardized communication protocol, enabling editors to offer rich language features like auto-completion, go-to-definition, syntax highlighting, and real-time diagnostics for OpenTofu HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) files. This means developers gain an IDE-like experience directly within their preferred text editor (e.g., VS Code, Neovim, Emacs), streamlining IaC development. OpenTofu, as an open-source, community-driven fork of Terraform, benefits from this integration by making its powerful declarative infrastructure management more accessible and efficient for engineers. The tofu-ls (OpenTofu Language Server) project is actively developed to provide these features, ensuring a smooth and productive workflow for managing cloud and on-premises resources.

abstract: AI workloads bring unique challenges to Adobe's goal of providing high-performance experiences to our customers, regardless of the capabilities of their devices or their distance from our datacenters. CDN based edge compute has been a tantalizing solution for AI workloads, but a truly portable solution across browsers and edge compute has been elusive. In this talk, we will discuss how to create a single Wasm component that can be run in wasmCloud and transpiled for use in the browser. We will then demonstrate the encoding of images using the open-source Trustmark watermark system in both the browser and CDN edge compute. This demonstration will use the wasi:webgpu interface from the WASI-GFX proposal, which enables graphics and GPU functionality outside the browser.

title: Applying DevSecOps Lessons To MLSecOps
abstract:
The transition from Development and Operations (DevOps) to Development, Security, and Operations (DevSecOps) revealed the need for security practices integrated into the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) to address critical software security gaps.

Now, developing and operating AI/ML applications introduces new dimensions of risk due to their dynamic behavior, inherent complexity, and often opaque decision-making processes. Unlike traditional software, ML models continuously evolve, requiring adaptive and ongoing security strategies tailored to AI/ML-specific challenges.

MLSecOps places a strong emphasis on integrating security practices within the ML development life cycle. It establishes security as a shared responsibility among ML developers, security practitioners, and operations teams. Embracing this methodology enables early identification and mitigation of security risks, facilitating the development of secure and trustworthy ML models.

title: Transparency Exchange API: Where To Find Product SBOM?
abstract:
Imagine you just bought a brand new smart light bulb. How would you find its SBOM? What about certifications, attestations, or other transparency artifacts? Now imagine needing that same information for a SaaS product, packaged software, or even a connected car.

Today, this kind of security metadata is fragmented, vendor-specific, and often hard to access, sometimes still exchanged by email. The OWASP Transparency Exchange API (TEA), an emerging Ecma standard, aims to solve this.

In this session, we'll explore how TEA is enabling a standardized, automated way to discover and access SBOMs / xBOMs, certifications, and other transparency artifacts across the software and hardware supply chain. We'll cover the motivation behind the standard, walk through the current specification and preview what’s next.

title: You Can Sign It, But Can You Trust It? Securing the Compilation Process
abstract:
Compilers run atop complex, interdependent stacks, making it hard to verify every component's integrity in each build. Existing CNCF projects (e.g., in-toto, Sigstore) primarily secure the upper layers of the supply chain, but do not verify the integrity of the entire underlying OS stack. Attacks like SolarWinds (2020) highlights the urgent need for stronger compilation process security.

This talk explores the challenges of securing the compilation process, and a proposed solution. A key challenge is that modern software stacks are deeply layered and interdependent, making it nearly impossible to verify every component involved. This talk rethinks how trust is established in software builds from build environment verifiability. The entire compilation process has been enclosed within a non-interactive SGX enclave and leveraging in-toto attestation to ensure that builds are verifiable. This talk offers a security enhancement for the CNCF ecosystem.

title: CANCELED Jarvis in the Cluster: Building Your K8s AI Assistant With Argo Events - Nic Vermande, ScaleOps
abstract:
What happens when Argo Events, Argo Workflows, and Tekton Pipelines join forces? We've created a Kubernetes automation system that doesn't just react, it anticipates. Our demo features "K8-Bit," a playful AI assistant that translates casual developer requests into sophisticated event chains and deployment workflows. Watch as a simple "ship it" command triggers intelligent repository analysis, custom pipeline assembly, and self-healing infrastructure responses.
In this session, we'll cover: event-driven architecture fundamentals, Argo Events' sensor/trigger model, live K8-Bit demonstrations, and practical integration patterns between Argo and Tekton. You'll learn how to build an event mesh spanning your entire delivery lifecycle that creates truly adaptive GitOps without sacrificing governance or declarative principles.

title: GitOps Meets AIOps: Building Reliable AI Pipelines With Argo
abstract:
As AI agents evolve from toy experiments to production-grade workflows, engineering teams face new orchestration challenges. LLM-based agents don't just need GPUs—they need state, retries, memory & coordination across tools, APIs, & data systems. Enter Argo: the battle-tested workflow engine that's quietly becoming the backbone of serious agentic infrastructure.

In this talk, we'll explore how Argo Workflows power the runtime execution of complex agent pipelines—chaining tasks, managing dependencies & scaling based on dynamic resource needs—while Argo CD provides GitOps-style control over the K8s infra and configurations those agents rely on. Together, they enable full lifecycle management: declarative deployment, dynamic execution, and safe rollbacks.

We'll also share how layering agents on top of Argo unlocks new capabilities—from safely iterating on prompt-driven pipelines, to automatically rolling back failed steps, to integrating observability and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

In this talk, we’ll walk through how we use this data and how teams can create their very own Lego Bricks and Sets, and how this model helps us standardise, scale, and simplify the developer journey across our organisation.

Expect practical takeaways for building your own version of Golden Paths with measurable impact.

title: LMCache: Lower LLM Performance Costs in the Enterprise
abstract: LLMs are powering copilots, search engines, document understanding, and chatbots. Most real-world AI apps route their workloads through GPU clusters running high-throughput inference engines. For enterprises however, the key concerns are still cost and return on investment (ROI). Welcome to LMCache, an open source LLM serving engine extension which reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) and increases throughput. In this talk, we’ll demonstrate how you can reduce GPU costs and token latency using LMCache. We'll demonstrate LMCache's high-performance KV cache management layer and its integration with well known production inference engines like vLLM and KServe, deployed on a Kubernetes cluster. We'll use real world examples like document analysis and high-speed RAG support. Get a glimpse into the growing community which is the OSS KV caching layer impacting ROI for companies like RedHat, IBM, Google, Nvidia, and CoreWeave.

title: From Chaos To Clarity: Debugging Microservices With Open Source Observability
abstract:
In the world of microservices, failures are inevitable—and figuring out why can feel like chasing shadows. Traditional debugging fails when requests span dozens of services, and you can't pause production to inspect what's happening.

In this demo-driven session, we'll walk through real-world failures and show how to make sense of the chaos using modern observability tools. We'll show basic logging, leverage Linkerd for problematic service interactions, utilize OpenTelemetry for end-to-end tracing and pinpointing failure points, and employ Prometheus to understand system health via metrics.

While we focus on these specific tools, the troubleshooting strategies shared are universally applicable to any cloud-native stack. Whether you're a platform engineer building reliable infrastructure or a developer fighting production fires, you'll gain concrete skills to make your microservices more observable and your on-call rotations much more manageable.

title: Windows Container Monitoring Demystified: OpenTelemetry in Action
abstract:
Struggling to monitor and debug Windows containers on Kubernetes? You’re not alone!
Unlike Linux, managing Windows workloads often feels like solving a puzzle with missing pieces. But it doesn’t have to be this way.
In this talk, we will show you how to implement a complete monitoring stack using Windows exporter on a Windows node in Kubernetes. We will explore the metric collectors in Windows Exporter, their functionalities, and practical use.
Next, we will deploy the Windows Exporter as a HostProcess pod, configuring a ServiceMonitor, and set up Prometheus to collect and visualize metrics.
Building on these capabilities, we will integrate open source observability tooling using OpenTelemetry. You’ll learn how to set up the Otel Collector, configure it for Windows metrics, and forward them to your observability backend.
Finally, we’ll elevate your debugging game by exploring the kubectl debug support for Windows nodes, enabling you to resolve issues faster at the node level.

To address these issues, the bank embarked on a journey to define and implement standardized technology stacks across the organization. By leveraging platform engineering, Itaú Unibanco created a unified platform that provided developers with consistent, reliable, and scalable environments.

This fragmentation forces application developers into a complex, inefficient dance of stitching together data from disparate sources, significantly hindering agility and developer experience. In addition, introducing new entities into this ecosystem is also expensive and time-consuming.

This presentation will unveil our journey in building a unified entity platform designed to revolutionize how LinkedIn manages and queries its vast data ecosystem. We'll walk through how we work with cross-functional teams spanning application, infrastructure, trust and tooling to build great experiences while abstracting complexity, and adoption success stories.

title: Running Databases in Istio's Service Mesh
abstract:
Think Istio is just for microservices? Think again! In this talk, you will hear a case study of GEICO's journey in developing our in-house database platform to leverage our Istio service mesh for security, service discovery and traffic management.

Kubernetes is an increasingly popular deployment target for databases, and in large organizations, standardization of tooling for networking, traffic management and security is key. Istio provides that standardization for stateless workloads, but with a little planning it can provide it for your stateful workloads, too. We'll discuss the nuances of running Apache Cassandra and Postgresql on Kubernetes, and the challenges we encountered building our next-generation database platform on top of our multi-cluster Istio service mesh.

Through a live walkthrough from environment setup to automated deployment, you’ll learn how to solve problems like duplicated config, inconsistent tool versions, unclear ownership, brittle CI pipelines, and out-of-date documentation. Instead of cobbling together scripts or relying on tribal knowledge, we’ll use proven open source tools to bring structure, automation, and clarity to your OpenTofu setup.

Whether you're breaking down a Tofulith, or scaling OpenTofu across a team, you’ll walk away with a repeatable model for managing infrastructure that’s more reliable, more collaborative, and more maintainable—one tool at a time.

abstract:

Wasm doesn’t spare you from needing robust solutions for crucial operational concerns like security, reliability, and observability, though – and without them, you’re not going to find much peace in production.

In this session, we’ll demonstrate how to integrate wasmCloud with Linkerd, bringing wasmCloud’s easy-to-use, self-hostable component orchestration capabilities with Linkerd’s lightweight, flexible security, reliability, and observability features. Join us for a quick dive into the capabilities of both these systems followed by a live demo showing how you can give your Wasm applications what they need to thrive in production – and what you need for your own peace of mind.

title: Panel: Cracking the Data Locality Puzzle
abstract:
Data transfer is slow -- so in AI and HPC, data locality matters. As workloads scale, optimizing where and how to run data-heavy workloads in Kubernetes becomes critical. Yet this area remains underexplored. The CNCF Batch Subproject shares findings from our work on data-locality-aware scheduling across clusters. Should we move compute to the data or the data to compute? What are the trade-offs in latency, cost, and efficiency?

We present methods to test potential policies: splitting jobs, exposing location-aware metadata from compute/storage, and basing scheduling on historical data and pricing. We share early discoveries from real-world tests across regions with limited bandwidth, storage, and power.

If your workloads are bottlenecked by data gravity -- or you’re chasing GPU efficiency across sites -- join us to explore emerging patterns for intelligent, cost-aware data placement in Kubernetes.

title: The State of Git Security With SLSA and Gittuf
abstract:
Git security has traditionally been a job given to forge platforms, utilizing features not built into Git itself. Systems such as gittuf introduced the ability to declare a security policy for a repository, independent of any forge platform, also independently verifiable by anybody with access to the repository. However, Git security goes much further than write access. What if there’s data on your repository that you’d only like certain people to read while still taking advantage of the version control features Git provides? How do we standardize gittuf into something that all security projects for Git can adopt and generate provenance for source code?

In this talk, we’ll discuss the state of Git security and how projects at the OpenSSF can help, such as gittuf and the SLSA Source Track. We’ll give an overview of both systems, and then delve deeper into what’s new with gittuf, such as read permissions for Git, efforts to standardize ideas from gittuf, and SLSA source provenance.

title: Threat Modeling for Kubernetes: Enhancing Security Posture in Complex and Regulated Environments
abstract:
Kubernetes environments are complex due to the number of potential third party integration such mesh solutions, secrets management, governance solutions and more. This complexity is increased especially for regulated entities like financial companies.

In this session, we’ll present a practical, non-traditional threat modeling approach tailored for Kubernetes. You’ll learn how to identify risks across clusters, workloads, and third-party components, and how to embed threat modeling into dev and SRE workflows.

We’ll also demonstrate how large language models (LLMs) can accelerate threat identification, map to MITRE ATT&CK, and support continuous security improvements.

You’ll leave with concrete strategies to operationalize threat modeling and strengthen your Kubernetes security posture.

title: Who Let the Agents Out? Securing AI Workflows the Right Way
abstract:
Agentic workflows in cloud-native environments demand robust identity and authorization. This session explores how to move beyond hard-coded credentials by assigning trusted, granular identities to agents acting on behalf of users. We'll dive into strategies for establishing traceability, enforcing least privilege, and enabling auditable decision-making within a zero-trust architecture.

Focusing on shared agents and tool-calling patterns, we'll demonstrate how SPIRE’s workload identity integrates with user identity to support secure delegation and dynamic, context-aware authorization. You’ll learn how to safeguard agent interactions with external tools and data sources through identity propagation and policy enforcement.

Through a real-world case study using Llama Stack and the extended Model Context Protocol (MCP), attendees will gain actionable insights to build secure, identity-aware agentic platforms ready for production use.

title: CANCELED ⚡Lightning Talk: From 0 To 200 Users; How Viasat Leverages Backstage To Drive IDP Adoption
abstract:
When starting the journey of building an Internal Developer Platform, one of the first question is often: "How do we get people to use it?"

In companies with larger engineering teams, the challenge of driving adoption can be daunting. Each team may have different reasons and incentives to use Backstage even if it's a directive from upper management. With deadlines still looming and the pressure to deliver, teams may not see the immediate value in adopting a new technology especially if it requires a change in their workflow or processes.

At Viasat, we found that the key to driving developer adoption of our Internal Developer Platform was to leverage Backstage as the portal and heavily buy into its plugin-based architecture. This talk will be telling the story of Viasat's journey of leveraging Backstage to build a portal that is not only functional but also user-friendly and team specific. The secret to engage our developers and encourage them to embrace the IDP is within the plugins.

title: Perception Data Pipeline Reconstruction With Argo Workflows
abstract:
A key research focus at the GAC R&D Center is autonomous driving. Fast and efficient data perception is fundamental to autonomous driving systems. However, managing their tasks — characterized by large-scale operations, high concurrency, and complex workflows — remains a critical challenge.
Since adopting Argo Workflows for platform reconstruction, we have developed an end-to-end data perception platform that orchestrates over 40,000 tasks daily and doubles task execution efficiency.
In this talk, we will share why Argo Workflows was chosen as our core orchestration solution and how we built large-scale pipelines across multiple scenarios, including data preprocessing, simulation, and offline inference. We will also discuss practical challenges and lessons learned in managing large-scale data perception pipelines, focusing on strategies for task concurrency optimization, file transfer acceleration, automatic GPU failure retries, GPU utilization improvement, and performance enhancement.

abstract:

At Priceline, we tackled this challenge by making the Pull Request the single UI for the full lifecycle of deployments.

Join us to learn how we integrated each Argo Project tool with PRs to create a custom experience without using Argo UIs. We’ll cover how we’ve utilized Argo Workflows, Argo CD, Argo Rollouts, and Argo Events to create a cohesive, developer-friendly deployment pipeline.

We’ll also discuss the problems we faced along the way, the solutions we developed to solve them, and the feedback we’ve received from developers on over 100K PRs.

title: The Hidden Foundation: How Effective Data Management Determines AI System Success
abstract:
Artificial intelligence systems are failing in production not because of algorithmic limitations, but due to fundamental data management failures that remain hidden beneath the surface. While organizations focus extensively on model selection and hyperparameter tuning, they often overlook the critical foundation that determines AI success: robust, reliable data management.

This talk will cover practical approaches for building resilient data foundations using cloud native technologies, including implementation patterns with OpenTelemetry for comprehensive data pipeline observability, Kubernetes & Kubeflow for management and orchestration, and Prometheus for monitoring data quality metrics at scale. The session addresses critical governance frameworks necessary for AI-ready data platforms, examining how organizations can establish sustainable data management practices that support both traditional workloads and AI applications.

title: From Data Overload To Optimized Insights: Implementing OTel Sampling for Smarter Observability
abstract:
Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry provides incredible insight into services, but can incur significant costs if not well managed. Sampling is a key part of an effective tracing rollout, yet its implementation can be challenging to set up and adopt.

Managing massive amounts of monitoring data from many interdependent services requires a flexible sampling solution, not a one-size-fits-all approach. The best sampling method depends on how your applications are deployed and how your observability system is designed. The key is to create a strategy that fulfills specific needs and provides the desired cost savings.

This case study examines the technical and cultural transformations required to implement open-source sampling components within a large enterprise setting. This session will address the deployment of these sampling components, the migration of end-users to sampling, and the resulting impact on data ingestion, offering insights applicable to your organization.

title: How To Trust a Liar: Instrumenting AI Execution With OpenTelemetry
abstract:
What happens when you build an open source, automated engineering journaling system from scratch, paired with an AI that’s all vibes and half-truths, while keeping its behavior observable? Well, this speaker did just that.

This talk showcases Commit Story, a background agent that triggers on each git commit, captures the developer–AI conversation, and generates an engineering journal entry— all while emitting correlated traces, logs, and metrics with OpenTelemetry. Here's the really cool part: the coding assistant can query this telemetry during development to reason about code using actual runtime evidence.

Through a real incident—an AI-powered function timing out—the session shows how development-time telemetry surfaced oversized inputs, ruled out a wrong theory, helped the agent avoid writing duplicate logic, and verified the fix.

The talk also acknowledges tradeoffs, has live demos throughout, and provides a link to software attendees can play with.

title: OpenTelemetry for Platform Engineers: Paving the Road To Self-Service Observability
abstract:
Platform engineers have a dual responsibility: keeping the infrastructure reliable and making observability effortless for developers. OpenTelemetry offers powerful, open-source standards that simplify these tasks - but knowing how to best leverage them can feel overwhelming. In this talk, we’ll demystify OpenTelemetry, with a practical focus on the Collector component, and explore how platform teams can build intuitive abstractions and automation.

You’ll learn how to deploy and configure the OpenTelemetry Collector, use it to provide centralized and scalable telemetry pipelines, and discover best practices for creating developer-friendly auto-instrumentation experiences. Through practical examples and lessons learned, you’ll leave empowered to provide your developers a frictionless path to comprehensive observability.

Platform teams invest heavily in "developer experience" yet struggle with adoption. Why? We focus on infrastructure while developers spend most of their time writing software, not deploying it.

This talk examines how platform engineering's infrastructure bias creates blind spots. Developers need local cloud API access, language-native libraries, and test data management - not just deployment pipelines. Some organizations are expanding platform scope: providing SDKs, enabling local workflows, automating test environments, even leveraging AI for cross-repository search.

You'll learn to identify gaps between what platforms provide and what developers actually need, see examples of platforms that moved "up the stack," and understand why broader scope drives adoption. It's time to expand our definition of platform engineering beyond CI/CD, Terraform and Kubernetes.

title: Scaling Flux at BT: A Multi-Cluster Telco Migration Journey
abstract:

Chris will share practical insights from this large-scale transformation, including how BT re-architected core network services—such as NetBox and other SDN tooling—to support continuous delivery. The talk will cover lessons learned from the initial migration, current challenges in managing stateful services, and upcoming plans to integrate Flagger for progressive delivery and Flux Operator to enable feature-branch testing and ephemeral environments.

Attendees will hear how BT enabled self-service developer environments, navigated both technical and cultural barriers, and developed a GitOps blueprint for GitOps adoption across a complex telco environment.

title: Is Zero-Downtime Migration Possible? Moving From Ingress & Sidecars To Gateway API
abstract:

Can we ensure traffic routing prioritizes locality to minimize latency and network costs? How can we maintain advanced observability using HTTP request metrics for autoscaling with KEDA, instead of relying solely on CPU or memory-based Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA)? And what about preserving request authentication and JWT validation? Can we continue to strengthen resilience between AI workloads and LLMs?

Join us on our real-world migration journey at Harri, as we transition our production environment from ingress controllers and sidecars to Kubernetes Gateway API and sidecar-less model. We'll share key discoveries, challenges, and lessons learned to help you plan a possible zero-downtime migration.

Through live demonstrations, we'll explore how to integrate OpenFeature's API into your CI/CD pipeline for progressive rollouts. Attendees will also learn practical techniques for automating feature releases based on metrics, implementing instant rollbacks, and leveraging OpenTelemetry integration for comprehensive observability. We'll examine how to monitor feature flag performance, track user impact, and make data-driven decisions about rollouts using modern observability tools.

The addition of multiple layers of safeguards are also employed to evaluate resource compliance at creation time as well as continual scanning to catch defects and drive continuous improvement. We will explore the main options for approaching these in the Kubernetes ecosystem and discuss the limitations and possible benefits of each approach. Is WASM viable today? Should we benefit from Knative feature limiting in-flight requests? Or can we go with a vanilla autoscaling? The session will present a few simulations regarding different use cases suitable for each workload highlighting differences and attributes that make the solution a good fit in terms of performance, stability, and budget.

We will uncover the current blockers with non-WASM technologies and evaluate whether WASM can address them effectively today – or if it remains a promise for the future.

abstract:

Equally crucial, though, is the complex data management system it necessitates, as we are looking for seamless collection, storage, processing, and analysis of data, all in real-time. But what does building an effective data pipeline like that entail?

We will start with real-time data ingestion. We'll cover what challenges one can face and how to overcome them using Apache Pulsar, a potent cloud-native event streaming platform. Then, we shift our focus downstream to perform analysis using online Machine Learning techniques & a stateful cloud-native stream processing engine (such as Bytewax or RisingWave).
